sections.title: Representative Cases
content: Waterpark Industry - Represented a large waterpark in Kansas City that involved national media coverage due to a fatality of a patron on one of the waterpark rides. Able to resolve the matter within four months of the date of the incident.
Hotel Industry - Represented a national hotel where an individual was shot by a security guard, that was an off-duty police officer.
Restaurant Industry - Represented a well-known and successful Plaza restaurant that exploded due to a gas leak.

Firearm Industry - Represented a firearm dealer who was sued after a pistol was used in a shooting of a family member. The case involved federal issues and was argued in front of the Missouri Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Oliver P. Maguire
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Oliver is an experience trial attorney, who has represented clients in courtrooms across the country. Licensed to practice in Kanas, Missouri, and several federal districts, Oliver has represented individuals, small businesses, large corporations, and insurance carriers in a wide variety of matters, such as landlord tenant disputes, unlawful detainers, breach of contract, copyright infringement, and auto accidents. From initial evaluation to appellate briefing, Oliver is experienced in all stages of litigation.

Oliver began practicing law in southwest Missouri, handling corporate matters and civil litigation in a largely rural setting. Oliver then moved his practice to the Kansas City Metropolitan Area, joining a multi-office, multi-state law firm. Practicing from Overland Park, Kansas, Oliver gained valuable insight into the operation of the distinct Kansas and Missouri court systems. In 2022, Oliver joined Knight Nicastro MacKay, LLC, practicing in its Kansas City, Missouri office. Oliver continues to provide excellent representation to his clients on both sides of the state line.

Outside of the office, Oliver enjoys spending time with his wife and three small children. On the weekends, you can see Oliver volunteering at Holy Trinity Catholic Church or watching a baseball game at Kauffman Stadium with his family.

attorneys.bio:
I have dedicated my career to representing the legal rights of injured individuals, and it is a privilege to have the opportunity each day to pursue justice on behalf of good people who are encountering difficult circumstances.

I am a native of St. Louis, Missouri, where I grew up with the goal of becoming a lawyer. I attended college at Webster University in St. Louis where I earned a B.A. in English, cum laude, and was a four-year member of the women's soccer team. I earned my J.D. from the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Law in 2011, where I served as the Articles & Symposia Editor of the UMKC Law Review.

For the past several years, I have represented individuals in employment and personal injury matters in Kansas City and St. Louis. There are many aspects of practicing law that I love, but nothing feels more satisfying than witnessing a client's sincere gratitude upon achieving justice on his or her behalf.

A respected attorney once told her “Caring makes this job hard, but caring is what makes you good at what you do,” and she’s kept those impactful words with her over the years. Sara is a compassionate advocate, having been the voice of children, victims of abuse, and people that are simply trying to hold on to what’s most dear to them. Within that compassion is a skilled, very capable attorney who will be exactly what’s needed in the courtroom.

Sara is the Managing Partner of Marler Law Partners. While she has the ability and does work on many of the varying cases through the firm, she lends a majority of her expertise to Family Law cases.

When she is not practicing law, Sara can be found trying to keep up with her two daughters or chasing after her three dogs.

attorneys.name: William Marsh
attorneys.practice_type: Firearms Offenses Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
None of us should only be judged by our worst day. We have all, at some point, faced the injustice of a wrongful accusation—whether criminal or not. Some of us simply make personal choices that the state has unjustifiably outlawed. Whatever the case may be, we all need an advocate, and Bill Marsh has been proud to assume that role for more than 15 years.

Bill started his career in 2009 and has only ever practiced law as a criminal defense attorney. Over the last decade-and-a-half, he has witnessed a criminal legal system that is often driven by hysteria and recognizes the crucial need for a strong buffer between the State and the Accused. As a respected litigator in St. Louis, Bill has successfully tried dozens of cases to juries and had countless others dismissed through an aggressive motions practice.

While Bill has represented thousands of clients in state court, more than half of his practice involves defending federal defendants. As the Director of Federal Practice at Kessler Williams, he knows the intricacies of this very specialized area of law—a minefield that can lead to disastrous unforeseen consequences for those who lack proper expertise. Bill prides his ability to help clients navigate this complex system and obtain the best outcomes possible. This often involves acquiring downward variance sentences, including supervisory terms when the federal sentencing guidelines have recommended significant prison time.

Over the last decade-and-a-half, Bill has learned that mitigation can be just as important as litigation. As a skilled storyteller, he knows how to present his clients to judges and prosecutors as nuanced human beings who are ultimately good at their core. His work has also taught him to understand addiction and its role in the lives of people who become ensnared in the system. While Bill believes substance use should be treated as a public health issue, he is intimately familiar with the various diversionary approaches courts have adopted in a partial (and often begrudging) concession that the War on Drugs has failed. Through these avenues, he has helped numerous clients circumvent the system outright.

Bill firmly believes that the criminal legal system cannot function without good defense lawyers. Therefore, he devotes significant time to mentoring and educating young lawyers and law students. In addition to teaching a yearly trial skills program to students at Emory University School of Law, Bill regularly presents to lawyers throughout Missouri on topics ranging from trial advocacy to the complex interplay between state and federal criminal law.

attorneys.name: Phillip Reed Martens
attorneys.practice_type: Sexual Abuse Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
About Reed Martens

Reed Martens is a dedicated trial lawyer and unwavering advocate for victims of sexual abuse and personal injury. Known for achieving successful verdicts and settlements, he has earned a strong reputation in the courtroom, where he has skillfully served as both lead and co-counsel on numerous cases.

Championing Survivors of Sexual Abuse

Helping survivors seek justice is at the heart of Reed’s practice. He approaches every case with empathy and determination, guiding victims through the legal process and holding both individuals and institutions accountable. Reed is committed to leaving no avenue unexplored in the pursuit of justice for his clients.

Beyond the Courtroom

Family is Reed’s greatest priority. He treasures spending time with his wife and three children, whether they’re enjoying the outdoors, relaxing at home, or creating new family memories. His devotion as a husband and father reflects the same core values that drive his advocacy—protecting and fighting for those who cannot fight for themselves.

Reed also embraces personal and professional challenges with the same energy he brings to his legal work. He completed the Ironman 70.3 in Panama City Beach alongside his Monsees & Mayer colleagues, Ryan Frazier and Chip Lee, demonstrating his commitment to perseverance, focus, and hard work. Outside of training, he enjoys hunting, fishing, and playing golf—pursuits that, like the practice of law, require strategy, discipline, and an unwavering drive to succeed.

attorneys.bio:
Stephen A. Martin is a skilled attorney with more than 30 years of legal experience, representing clients in a variety of general practice areas, including the areas of civil litigation, real estate law, business law, municipal law and estate planning.

Prior to starting his own firm, he was a partner at Barklage, Brett, Martin, Wibbenmeyer & Hamill, P.C., served as County Counselor for St. Charles County and prior to that, County Counselor for Clay County. Kylee R. Mattoon is a cum laude graduate of Washington University School of Law. Kylee earned her bachelor’s degree in Human Development & Family Studies from the University of Missouri, graduating summa cum laude. attorneys.bio:
David was born and raised in Kansas City, where he attended Rockhurst High School. He went on to Boston College and earned a double major in Political Science and Economics. Upon returning to Kansas City, David enrolled at the University of Missouri - Kansas City Law School, where he received the American Jurisprudence Award and was a Victor Wilson Scholar.

David's practice concentrates on safety of children and the elderly. David has helped many clients recover for injuries or damages they received, including handicapped children who have been neglected or abused; children injured by dangerous conditions in stores; injury and death to the elderly from negligent nursing homes and transportation companies; injuries at swimming facilities; various automobile claims against negligent drivers.

For these efforts, David has been admitted to the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. He has received the top rating of AV for a lawyer by Martindale-Hubbell and has been named one of the Top 100 Trial Lawyers by the American Trial Lawyers Association and the American Society of Legal Advocates. The American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys recognized David as one of the top 10 best lawyers in Missouri for client satisfaction.

David volunteers his time for legal aid programs throughout Missouri and Kansas, and serves on the Board of various not-for-profit charity organizations.

attorneys.name: Connor McAteer
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Connor McAteer is a civil trial lawyer with a caring and client-oriented approach. He focuses his practice on a range of personal injury matters, including claims involving car accidents, premises accidents, and serious personal injuries.

Drawn to the practice of law by his interest in advocacy and public service, Connor has always been passionate about standing up for others and helping convey their stories in compelling and persuasive ways. On his journey to becoming a lawyer, he attended the University of Missouri, where he earned his undergraduate degree in Business Administration with a Minor in Psychology. The University of Missouri also awarded him two certificates: the Dispute Resolution Certificate and the Multicultural Certificate. Connor next attended the University of Missouri School of Law, where he earned his Juris Doctor.

As a trial attorney at DM Injury Law, Connor takes a personalized approach that’s driven by his commitment to serving his clients’ best interests, providing legal expertise, and guiding clients through the complexities of the legal process. He believes the client-attorney relationship is one built on trust, communication, and a shared goal of seeking justice and fair compensation.

In his practice, Connor has cultivated a reputation for both his legal insight and his client-focused approach. He takes the time to establish open channels of communication with those he represents and to foster an environment where clients feel comfortable discussing their situations, needs, and objectives. He also invests time in helping clients understand what they can expect of the process and how to appropriately manage their expectations. In all matters, he strives to achieve the best possible results for his clients given their unique circumstances.

Connor grew up in Peoria, Illinois, and attended Mizzou for undergrad and law school. He enjoys reading, snowboarding, and staying active, and since moving to Kansas City, trying new local restaurants.

attorneys.name: Ted J. McDonald
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Ted J. McDonald practices in a variety of areas of civil litigation with a primary emphasis on defending and consulting long term care and assisted living facilities. Ted serves as counsel for some of the largest providers of long term care services in the country. Mr. McDonald’s background includes experience in products liability, medical malpractice and personal injury litigation.

Mr. McDonald earned his undergraduate degree in business from the University of Kansas. He received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Missouri at Kansas City.

Mr. McDonald is a member of both the Missouri and Kansas Bars and is admitted to practice in the United States District Courts in Missouri and Kansas.

Ted is a member of the International Association of Defense Counsel (IADC) and holds numerous positions of leadership with the Defense Research Institute (current member, DRI Law Institute; past Chair, DRI Medical Liability and Healthcare Law Committee; past Chair, DRI Nursing Home-ALF Subcommittee; past member, DRI Governance Committee; past Chair, DRI Young Lawyers’ Committee; past Faculty, DRI Nursing Home and Medical Liability Seminars). Mr. McDonald has been published in DRI and IADC publications.

Ted is a member of the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association (past, Chair Public Service Committee), Johnson County Bar Association, and the Kansas Defense Lawyers Association.

Mr. McDonald in is active in his community, currently serving as the Kansas State Coordinator (working together with Kansas Supreme Court Chief Justice Lawton Nuss) for iCivics, a national program founded by Justice Sandra Day O’Connor designed to educate school children about three branches of government and civic duty. Mr. McDonald is the past Chairman of the Board of Folds of Honor (Kansas City Chapter), a national philanthropic organization founded by Major Dan Rooney, a U.S. Air Force Pilot and former PGA golfer, which awards educational scholarships to the families of injured/fallen service men and women.

attorneys.name: Timothy M McDuffey
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Osage Beach, MO
attorneys.bio:
Tim McDuffey has been practicing law since graduating from law school in 1994. He has been a Partner at Bergmanis & McDuffey, L.L.C. since 1998. His primary emphasis of practice is litigation. Tim has prepared and tried Personal Injury, Wrongful Death, Workers Compensation and Social Security Disability cases on behalf of injured parties.

Prior to going to law school, Tim attended Missouri State University, graduating with high honors. He played on two championship football teams at SMS, and received All-American honors. Tim also excelled academically, and received numerous awards for his academic achievements, including, being named to the GTE, Division I, Academic All-American team and being named the Outstanding Student Athlete for SMS University in 1991.

Tim attended Law School at the University of Missouri-Columbia. His grades placed him in the top ten percent of his class. He was named to the University's prestigious Law Review and was also the Recipient of the School's Professional Ethics Award.

Tim has also been active in the Missouri Bar, serving on the Young Lawyers Section Council since 2000. He has further served as a Member of the Missouri Board of Governors during the years of 2001 and 2002. Tim has lectured and written on various aspects of representing Claimants under the Missouri Workers Compensation Law.

attorneys.name: Kevin J. McManus
attorneys.firm_name: Kevin McManus Law: Kansas City Personal Injury & Accident Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Kevin McManus was born and raised in Kansas City, and has spent his career practicing law in courts throughout Missouri and Kansas. Kevin became a lawyer because he believed in the power of our legal system to improve both clients’ lives and the community as a whole. This core belief motivates his legal practice and his commitment to community service. After graduating law school, Kevin worked for a national law firm based in Kansas City, where he represented large corporations and insurance companies in a variety of complex legal matters. Early in his career, Kevin was contacted by a young lady who suffered a brain injury in a car crash. Ultimately, Kevin was able to help her obtain a favorable settlement that allowed her not just to recover from her injuries but also to build a better future. Since that time, Kevin has devoted his career to helping others who have been injured or wronged receive the justice they deserve through personal injury and disability law. His firm has helped countless individuals throughout Missouri and Kansas and is focused on educating and empowering clients with high-quality legal service and representation. In addition to practicing law, Kevin McManus served on the City Council for Kansas City, Missouri for two (2) terms from 2015 to 2023, and as Mayor Pro Tem, which required him to perform official duties in the absence of the Mayor. Prior to that, he served in the Missouri House of Representatives. These experiences have given him keen insight into the laws at issue and the opportunity to serve our greater community.

More About Kevin Outside of Injury & Disability Law

A native of Kansas City, Kevin earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Notre Dame and his law degree with honors from Saint Louis University. He resides with his wife and their two sons in Kansas City, Missouri.

attorneys.name: Bridget McManus
attorneys.firm_name: Kevin McManus Law: Kansas City Personal Injury & Accident Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Bridget McManus: A Dedicated Advocate for Clients in Need

Bridget McManus is a compassionate and experienced attorney dedicated to helping clients navigate the often stressful and overwhelming aftermath of an accident or disability. With over 25 years of legal experience in both private and public sectors, Bridget brings a wealth of knowledge and a passion for advocating for those who need it most. Her primary focus is on managing and settling cases prior to litigation, ensuring clients receive the treatment, support, and compensation they deserve.

A Role Built on Compassion and Connection

At the heart of Bridget’s work is her commitment to building strong relationships with her clients. She understands that being involved in a legal case can be daunting, and she strives to ease that burden by maintaining clear and open communication. Bridget takes the time to get to know each client personally, working with them to facilitate their treatment and guiding them through the process from start to settlement. Her goal is always to reduce her clients’ stress and help them achieve the best possible outcome.

Bridget also leverages her experience in developing productive relationships with insurance adjusters, ensuring that cases move swiftly toward resolution. Her approach is rooted in the belief that clients should always feel supported and informed throughout their legal journey. In a world where it’s often difficult to get a live person on the phone, Bridget takes pride in being accessible and present for her clients every step of the way.

The Path to Advocacy

Bridget’s path to becoming an attorney was driven by a deep-seated desire to help people. Early in her career, she served as a public defender, representing individuals facing incredibly difficult circumstances. This experience reinforced the importance of thorough investigation, clear communication, and strategic case management — skills that she has carried with her throughout her career.

Her time working for the Missouri Court of Appeals also gave her unique insight into protecting clients’ rights during trial and navigating appellate matters when necessary. This experience has made Bridget especially skilled at anticipating legal challenges and strategically positioning her clients for the best possible outcomes.

When the opportunity arose to join her brother, Kevin McManus, at the firm, Bridget knew it was the right fit. She was drawn to the firm’s positive, team-oriented culture and its clear mission to advocate for clients and their families. Knowing that she could combine her experience, passion for helping others, and commitment to client care in a supportive work environment solidified her decision.

A Life Beyond the Office

Outside of the office, Bridget’s most cherished role is being a mom to her 11-year-old son. She spends much of her free time cheering him on at baseball and basketball games, volunteering at his grade school, and even coaching his Battle of the Books team. Bridget loves being an active and involved parent, and she finds joy in creating memorable experiences with her son.

Bridget is also an avid sports fan, particularly devoted to Kansas City’s beloved Chiefs and Royals. She’s eagerly anticipating the upcoming baseball season, with favorite players like Salvador Perez and Bobby Witt Jr. keeping her excitement high. In addition to her love for sports, Bridget is a distance runner currently training for her third half-marathon. When she’s not running or spending time with her family, she enjoys painting — a hobby that recently led to creating a humorous portrait of Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift for a white elephant gift exchange.

Words to Live By

A guiding principle that influences both Bridget’s professional and personal life is the understanding that “everyone is going through something.” This perspective shapes the empathy and care she extends to her clients, colleagues, and loved ones alike. Her ability to approach each case and client with understanding and compassion is a direct reflection of her belief that everyone deserves to be heard, supported, and treated with kindness.

An Advocate, A Teammate, A Difference-Maker Bridget McManus is more than just an attorney — she is a fierce advocate, a compassionate listener, and a problem-solver dedicated to making a difference. Her diverse legal background, combined with her genuine care for people, makes her an invaluable member of the firm. Every case she handles is approached with the same dedication: to provide unwavering support, clear guidance, and the best possible resolution for her clients.

At her core, Bridget thrives on helping people rebuild their lives after an accident or disability. She believes that through compassion, clear communication, and diligent advocacy, she can turn what often feels like a dark time in her clients’ lives into a path toward hope and healing.

attorneys.name: Patrick D. McMurtray
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Webster Groves, MO
attorneys.bio:
Patrick McMurtray has spent nearly 40 years as an attorney developing experience and skills to navigate complex litigation. His first 20 years of law practice were almost exclusively on the defense side, including work as regional and national counsel in tens of thousands of cases throughout the United States. Since then, Patrick has used the insights he gained to understand and complement his litigation experience. He has developed a national practice representing plaintiffs in significant environmental, pharmaceutical, medical device, and other complex litigation. He also has considerable experience representing business owners and shareholders in various disputes.

Patrick graduated from Ole Miss Law School in 1984 and attended undergraduate school there. He returned to the United States in 2012 from China, where part of his work involved consulting with Chinese law firms and businesses on various issues. Since his return to the U.S., he has become active in the community, including his work as a reserve deputy and a volunteer fire department member, in addition to providing pro bono legal representation to various charitable organizations.

Patrick has been admitted to practice in Tennessee since 2014, Mississippi since 1984, Alabama since 1992, and Louisiana since 1993. He is a Martindale-Hubbell AV-rated attorney and is admitted to the Supreme Courts of Alabama, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Tennessee, as well as the U.S. Court of Federal Claims, various U.S. Federal district courts, and courts of appeal.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Martindale-Hubbell AV-rated Attorney

attorneys.name: Elizabeth McNulty
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
At The Simon Law Firm, P.C., located in St. Louis, Missouri, attorney Elizabeth McNulty is a fervent champion for her clients, always ready to go above and beyond to secure the most favorable outcomes. Her practice spans nationwide, tackling personal injury cases such as product liability, medical malpractice and class actions.

A consummate professional through and through, Ms. McNulty is committed to holding individuals and entities responsible for the harm they inflict. Her clients often turn to her during challenging times, seeking the guidance and solutions she tirelessly provides when they need them most.

Ms. McNulty’s journey into law began while clerking at The Simon Law Firm, P.C., during her time at the Washington University School of Law. This role offered her invaluable exposure to cases involving defective products, medical malpractice and personal injuries, alongside some of the most esteemed legal minds. She is authorized to practice law in Missouri, Illinois and Kansas, and she is admitted to the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Missouri.

Since childhood, Ms. McNulty has been drawn to the legal field, her love for debate sparked by playful arguments with her older brother. Her mother once envisioned them opening law firms across from each other, engaging in friendly rivalry – a dream partially realized as they both pursued legal careers in different cities.

For Ms. McNulty, her passion for debate has evolved into a steadfast determination to assist others in rectifying injustices. She values the role of a trusted advocate for her clients. Recognized as an Up & Coming Attorney by Missouri Lawyers Media, included in Best Lawyers’ Ones to Watch list and a former president of the Women’s Lawyers Association of Greater St. Louis (2023-2024), she continues to make her mark in the legal world.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Patrick McPhail is a staunch advocate for his clients in the strenuous legal challenges they face, and he utilizes every legal tool in his arsenal to help them achieve their goals with precision and grace. At The Simon Law Firm, P.C., in St. Louis, Missouri, he primarily handles personal injury law, such as cases involving medical malpractice, defective products and class actions, as well as business litigation.

Attending the St. Lawrence University School of Law, Mr. McPhail took full advantage of the opportunities he was presented with, including being closely involved with the St. Lawrence University Law Journal and the Moot Court Appellate Lawyers Association Competition. He received his Juris Doctor in 2017, and in the same year, he obtained his license to practice law in Missouri. Prior to enrolling in law school, he completed his undergraduate studies at Southern Illinois University in Edwardsville, graduating with his Bachelor of Science degree in 2014.

Soon after becoming licensed in Missouri, Mr. McPhail gained admission to practice in Illinois and before the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Missouri, the United States District Court for the Western District of Arkansas, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, the Supreme Court of Missouri and the United States Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit.

A consummate professional through and through, Mr. McPhail strives to provide his clients with the top-quality advocacy they deserve after enduring personal hardship due to the reckless actions of another. For his many contributions, he has been included in Best Lawyers’ Ones to Watch list for his work in medical malpractice law, personal injury litigation and products liability litigation. Within his legal community, he is a member of The Bar Association of Metropolitan St. Louis.

attorneys.name: Alexander C. Melin
attorneys.practice_type: Complex and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Alexander C. Melin is an attorney at Edgar Law Firm LLC, in Kansas City, Missouri since joining the Firm in early 2023. Alexander brings a wealth of litigation experience and a passion for justice to his work at the Firm. Alexander represents clients in a broad array of areas, including complex commercial disputes and fraud cases.

In his five years prior to joining the Firm, Alexander worked in Kansas City law firms in the areas of plaintiffs' personal injury and insurance bad faith, helping those harmed by the negligence and the wrongdoing of others. Prior to moving to Kansas City in 2017, Alexander worked as an Assistant Ford County Attorney in Ford County, Kansas. Before that, he began his career at a general practice in southwest Kansas where he was exposed to a wide variety of practice areas.

A native Kansan, Alexander attended the University of Kansas, in Lawrence, Kansas, graduating in the top ten percent of his class in 2006 with a B.A. in Slavic Languages and Literature. Alexander went on to earn his M.A. in Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies there in 2008. Alexander subsequently studied law at the University of Kansas School of Law, graduating with his J.D. in the top ten percent of his class in 2014. While he was in law school, Alexander interned with the Finney County Attorney in Garden City, Kansas, and with the American Chamber of Commerce in the Republic of Georgia.

Alexander is married and has a daughter. He enjoys spending time with his family and friends, playing chess, studying languages, reading, and traveling.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Hardy C. Menees is a partner at the law firm of Menees & Menees, located in Kirkwood, Missouri. Mr. Menees practices in various areas of civil litigation including family law and personal injury. He represents clients in the St. Louis, Missouri, metropolitan area and the surrounding counties, including St. Louis County.

Mr. Menees handles domestic cases, including those involving high-asset divorce and custody. In addition, he takes on matters involving medical malpractice and wrongful death, as well as some select general personal injury cases. He has over 40 years of legal experience and is a seasoned negotiator and trial lawyer.

In addition to his private practice, Mr. Menees is a city attorney and prosecuting attorney for the city of St. John, Missouri. Mr. Menees serves as an adjunct faculty member at St. Louis University School of Law. He is an active member of The Missouri Bar and the Illinois State Bar Association. He holds licenses to practice law in both states and before the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit.

Mr. Menees graduated cum laude from Princeton University with a bachelor’s degree. He earned his law degree from Washington University School of Law in St. Louis. He received his license to practice law in 1977.

attorneys.name: Henry M. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, Henry “Hank” Miller has expertly represented clients in family law matters, including those with complex assets in high net worth. He handles any type of Missouri family law related matters, including:

Divorces – Contested and Uncontested

Paternity cases – Contested and Uncontested

Child custody – Original Actions and Motions to Modify

Child support – Original Actions, Motions to Modify and Enforcement Actions

Juvenile Law – Abuse and Neglect and Delinquency Cases

Domestic Violence- Orders of Protection

Guardianships and Adoptions

Step-Parent Adoptions

LGBTQ issues including the subjects above and name and gender marker changes.

Hank and his firm have the resources and experience to aggressively litigate even the most complicated cases. He has successfully tried many cases. He also has extensive training in mediation and works hard to see if a case can be amicably resolved before the case becomes a battle. The hope in any family law case is that a reasonable settlement can be reached as quickly and at the lowest cost possible. This is especially true when kids are involved. As tempting as it may be to want to launch an all-out assault against the other party, parents owe it to their kids to remain reasonable with each other and do their very best to make sure the kids see an image of mutual respect between the parents. Whatever the parents may think of each other, to the kids they are Mom and Dad, and the kids deserve to be encouraged and allowed to love each of their parents.

Hank also acts as a parent coordinator and serves as a Guardian Ad Litem in divorce cases, representing the best interest of the child. He was selected for inclusion in Super Lawyers, Missouri and Kansas in 2015 and every year since.

Hank was born and raised in St. Louis, and continues to live here with his wife and two sons.

attorneys.name: Janelle Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Pre-Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Janelle Miller is a personal injury attorney at DM Injury Law, where she leverages her insight as a former prosecutor to provide skilled and client-focused representation to clients from our Topeka office. She focuses her areas of practice on auto accidents, premises liability, and other personal injury matters.

Janelle grew up in Topeka, Kansas, with a mother who served as a union steward. Inspired by watching her mother fight for her coworkers, she became enamored with the art of advocacy and made it her mission while she was still in elementary school to become a lawyer so she could help others just like her mom. Her first foray into the law came in high school when she served as an intern for the Attorney General’s Consumer Protection Division. She then went on to earn her undergraduate degree from Washburn University and her law degree from the University of Missouri, Kansas City School of Law.

Following law school, Janelle began her legal career representing the State of Missouri as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney. From there, she became an Assistant District Attorney in Shawnee County, Kansas, and later represented the State of Kansas, specifically the Kansas Department of Children and Family Services, as a Contract Attorney.

Now a committed Plaintiffs’ Attorney, Janelle leverages her extensive trial experience as a former prosecutor to help position her clients for success in a range of personal injury cases. She is known for her personalized and passionate approach and prides herself on taking the necessary time to listen to her clients, empathize with their situations, and help them understand their rights under the law. In every case she handles, she places herself in her clients’ shoes and leaves no stone unturned in pursuing the compensation they deserve.

Dan served as vice president of his fraternity at Mizzou.

After graduating from Mizzou in 1994, Dan was accepted to the University of Missouri School of Law in Columbia, Missouri. During law school, Dan worked as a law clerk at the firm of Oliver, Walker and Wilson in Columbia, Missouri. During this time Dan began learning the fundamental elements of insurance litigation, workers' compensation and family law. Dan assisted Art Oliver, Roland Walker and Betty Wilson with various projects. Dan even assisted Art Oliver with an automobile accident trial. Dan regards his law clerk experience at Oliver, Walker and Wilson as absolutely invaluable.

Dan earned several awards during law school. No other award is more cherished by Dan that the Order of Barristers. The Order of Barristers is given to only ten students in each graduating class. It is for excellence in moot court. During law school Dan showed his proficiency in the courtroom by winning the regional moot court competition. While in law school Dan also received the R. David Ray Award for Trial Advocacy and the Roscoe Anderson award for Excellence in Moot Court.

Dan graduated from law school in 1997 and later joined Oliver, Walker, Wilson as an associate attorney. In August of 1998 Dan accepted a new position as an attorney with the law firm of Inglish and Monaco, P.C. in Lake Ozark, Missouri. After working for three years with Lewis Bridges and Tim Cisar in the Lake Ozark office of Inglish and Monaco, Dan, Lew and Tim decided to form their own practice.

In November of 2001 Bridges, Cisar and Mizell, LLC opened for business. Dan was extremely proud to be a named partner in his own law firm. Bridges, Cisar and Mizell, LLC initially practiced out of the Cliffside Center in Lake Ozark. However, the success of the firm allowed Bridges, Cisar and Mizell, LLC to build its own law office building in 2004. Bridges, Cisar and Mizell, LLC moved into the new space at 750 Bagnell Dam Boulevard in Lake Ozark in October of 2004.

Dan's practice continued to grow throughout the first decade of the new millennium. Dan has always accepted automobile accident cases, workers' compensation cases, boat accident cases, slip and fall claims, wrongful death claims and other tort claims.

Dan and his family decided to relocate to Lebanon, Missouri in May of 2007. Dan purchased Darrell Deputy's law office at 120 East Second Street in Lebanon, Missouri in June, 2007. After careful deliberation, Darrell and Dan entered into an agreement whereby Dan would purchase Darrell's law practice. While Darrell continues to actively practice law in Lebanon, it is Darrell's intention to slowly and gracefully transition to a more limited role in Deputy and Mizell.

Under Dan's management of Deputy and Mizell, LLC the firm has grown exponentially. 2008 saw the opening of a new location at 16 Camden County Northeast in Camdenton, Missouri. In 2011 the firm purchased Kerry Rowden's law practice in Tuscumbia, Missouri. Kerry Rowden became the Associate Circuit Judge in Maries County, Missouri.

If you have been involved in any type of incident where you suffered bodily injury due to the negligence of another, you should contact Dan Mizell for a free consultation.

Dan is a member of the Missouri Bar, the Laclede County Bar Association and is a fellow of the Missouri Bar Foundation.

Dan has been married to his wife Jenny since 1993. They have two young children, Katie and Missy. Dan and Jenny reside in Lebanon, Missouri.

attorneys.name: Barry Moore
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Barry Moore brings a unique blend of experience and passion to the Goldblatt + Singer team, combining his background in sales management and drywall contracting with his dedication to client advocacy. Licensed to practice law in Missouri, Illinois, the Central District of Illinois, and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri, Barry is committed to guiding clients through the most challenging times in their lives.

Having received the profound advice that, “Even though this is what we do every day for hundreds of people, for each individual, this is the most important issue in their life until we get them a resolution,” Barry takes this to heart in every case. His empathetic and client-centered approach ensures that every person he represents feels heard and supported.

Barry’s passion lies in being a voice for individuals who find themselves in situations they never imagined—whether facing legal challenges or seeking justice. His experience allows him to connect with clients on a personal level, offering practical insights and solutions tailored to their unique circumstances.

Outside of the courtroom, Barry enjoys spending time with his family and pursuing his love for golf. Originally from Collinsville, IL, he is proud to serve clients in both Missouri and Illinois, providing personalized legal representation that focuses on achieving the best possible outcomes.

If you’re looking for an attorney who combines real-world experience, legal expertise, and a genuine passion for people, Barry Moore is here to help you navigate the complexities of your case. Contact Barry today for a consultation and discover how he can be your voice in the legal process.

An active member in the community, Kyle enjoys networking and social opportunities through the Missouri Bar Young Lawyers Association, young professional associations, and local recreational sports organizations. He is also a member of the Missouri and Cole County Bars.

attorneys.name: Melanie Morgan
attorneys.firm_name: Morgan Pilate LLC Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Melanie began her career as a criminal defense lawyer while in law school at the University of Kansas School of Law where she was first an intern and then a student director at the Defender Project. While serving the Defender Project, Melanie became convinced that effective advocacy demands not only a sharp intellect but also a deep commitment to justice. Following her fervor of representing the criminally accused, Melanie started out as an attorney with the prominent criminal defense firm, the Law Office of Joseph D. Johnson, Chtd., before opening her own firm in 2002. Federal cases comprise the vast majority of Melanie's caseload and she regularly litigates a wide variety of criminal defense cases including drug and drug conspiracy charges, gun and firearm violations, robbery, sex and pornography offenses, immigration violations, and various types of fraud cases including check, wire, mortgage and tax. Melanie has a very active trial practice and is widely known for the passion and persuasiveness of her courtroom presentations. Recent acquittals include United States v. William Carter, United States v. Cortez Williams, United States v. Jacob Unrau and State of Kansas v. William McDonald.

Melanie's commitment to criminal defense extends beyond her own practice. She is the Immediate Past President of the Kansas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and consults with other lawyers on various legal matters. She has twice been invited to be part of the faculty of the prestigious National Criminal Defense College in Macon, Georgia. Melanie has also lectured on ethics and search and seizure issues.

attorneys.name: Timothy Riley Morgan Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Camdenton, MO
attorneys.bio:
Timothy Riley Morgan has been recognized for obtaining exceptional results for his clients for over a decade of representing people in states across the country. For the past 15 years Tim’s caseload has primarily focused on complex wrongful death and permanent injury cases involving defectively designed or manufactured products, semi-truck crashes, car crashes, and railroad crossing collisions.

Tim worked in his home town, Lexington, Missouri, for the law firm of Langdon & Emison in 2005, upon completing a judicial clerkship with the Honorable Thomas C. Clark in the Circuit Court of Jackson County where he also served as the bailiff.

During his time as a lawyer Tim has been an integral part of collecting more than $100 million dollars in verdicts and settlements. Tim and fellow lawyer Rob Sullivan were recognized by Missouri Lawyer’s weekly for obtaining one of the top 20 verdicts reported in 2006 for the entire State of Missouri. The case involved the wrongful death of a man due to defective brakes. In 2009, Tim was recognized as one of the top 40 lawyers under the age of 40, and as a “Rising Star” in the legal community of Missouri and Kansas by Missouri/Kansas Super Lawyers. Tim has been selected by his peers as a Super Lawyer in both Missouri and Kansas for several years in a row, which is awarded to 1% of the lawyers in the state. In 2014, Tim, Erik Bergmanis, and Rob Sullivan were recognized by Missouri Lawyer’s Weekly for obtaining a 15 million dollar verdict for their client, which was the largest verdict in the entire state of Missouri for the year of 2014, and the largest verdict ever reported in Camden County, which involved representing a burn victim who received life threatening injuries when his boat exploded into fire at a gas dock located on the Lake of the Ozarks. Tim and Erik Bergmanis first started working together on complex cases back in 2004 when they represented burn victims that were injured when a RV exploded into flames here at the Lake of the Ozarks.

Tim received his college degree in Psychology from the University of Missouri – Columbia and was member of the Phi Delta Theta fraternity. He next earned his Law Degree with Distinction from the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Law. He graduated 4th in his class of 186 people. His honors in law school included being a part of the Bench and Robe Honor Society at graduation, being chosen as a member of the Law Review, being chosen to be a recipient of the outstanding service award from the Johnson County Prosecutor’s office during his second year of law school, and receiving awards for obtaining the highest law school final exam score in two of his classes.

Tim has experience and helped obtain results in wrongful death and severe injury cases in several different states across the country against some of the largest corporations in the country, including General Motors, Ford Motor Company, Union Pacific Railroad, Toyota, Honda, Norfolk Southern railroad, CSX railroad, Brunswick Corporation, and others.

Tim played competitive basketball when he was in high school and junior college, he still enjoys playing basketball, tennis, and riding mountain bikes when he and his wife are not enjoying their time cheering for their three children during their sporting events, or, while they are fishing here at Lake of the Ozarks, where he and his wife have recently moved to raise their family.

In 2014, Tim, Erik Bergmanis, and Rob Sullivan were recognized by Missouri Lawyer’s Weekly for obtaining a 15 million dollar verdict for their client, which was the largest verdict in the entire state of Missouri for the year of 2014, and the largest verdict ever reported in Camden County, which involved representing a burn victim who received life threatening injuries when his boat exploded into fire at a gas dock located on the Lake of the Ozarks. Tim and Erik Bergmanis first started working together on complex cases back in 2004 when they represented burn victims that were injured when a RV exploded into flames here at the Lake of the Ozarks.

Tim received his college degree in Psychology from the University of Missouri – Columbia and was member of the Phi Delta Theta fraternity. He next earned his Law Degree with Distinction from the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Law. He graduated 4th in his class of 186 people. His honors in law school included being a part of the Bench and Robe Honor Society at graduation, being chosen as a member of the Law Review, being chosen to be a recipient of the outstanding service award from the Johnson County Prosecutor’s office during his second year of law school, and receiving awards for obtaining the highest law school final exam score in two of his classes.

Tim has experience and helped obtain results in wrongful death and severe injury cases in several different states across the country against some of the largest corporations in the country, including General Motors, Ford Motor Company, Union Pacific Railroad, Toyota, Honda, Norfolk Southern railroad, CSX railroad, Brunswick Corporation, and others.

Tim played competitive basketball when he was in high school and junior college, he still enjoys playing basketball, tennis, and riding mountain bikes when he and his wife are not enjoying their time cheering for their three children during their sporting events, or, while they are fishing here at Lake of the Ozarks, where he and his wife have recently moved to raise their family.

BPS v. Covington – Successful Daubert Motion on Plaintiff’s primary roofing expert. (2021)

Hawk Properties v. Allstate Insurance Company, St. Clair County, Illinois (2019) - Obtained a unanimous defense verdict for Allstate Insurance Company in St. Clair County Illinois on a first party property case involving a collapse of building. The insured had argued that the collapse was caused by a vehicle even though there was no evidence of this. Allstate took the position that the collapse was due to long term lack of maintenance and wear and tear.

Church Mutual Insurance v. Circle of Light, Eastern District of Missouri Federal Court (2019) – Obtained Summary Judgment in favor of Church Mutual. The court set aside an arguably binding $550,000 appraisal award holding the umpire and appraiser had not complied with the parties agreed upon appraisal guidelines. The court reaffirmed Missouri law that had not been utilized in 75 years.
Reich v. Allstate, Jackson County, Illinois (2018) – Jury awarded only a small percentage of the damages. Total exposure was $175,000.

Allstate Vehicle and Property Insurance Company v. James Graham, Jr., Eastern District of Missouri Federal Court (2017). Obtained a full defense verdict in an arson trial. The insured’s counsel asked the jury for more than $500,000. The jury returned a unanimous verdict in favor of the insurance company.

Williams v. Farm Bureau, Jackson County Circuit Court (2016). Obtained directed verdict in Jackson County, Missouri. Plaintiffs claimed more than $300,000 of personal property. Farm Bureau obtained a directed verdict, as plaintiffs did not make a submissible case on damages. The court’s directed verdict was upheld on appeal.

attorneys.name: Elaine Moss
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Moss focuses her practice on complex insurance coverage matters. She particularly enjoys her role as a trusted advisor to clients regarding policy development and risk transfer strategies. She handles complex coverage litigation throughout across the Midwest. She also serves as defense counsel on complex construction litigation. A Kansas native, Ms. Moss began her career with Crosby, Heafey, Roach, and May (now ReedSmith) in Los Angeles. While she enjoyed the challenge and experience of BigLaw, she was fortunate to have the opportunity to resettle in St. Louis to work on the Transit Casualty Receivership. Ms. Moss writes and speaks frequently on insurance-related topics, as well as diversity and inclusion issues. She particularly enjoys mentoring law students and young lawyers as they embark on their legal careers. She also frequently consults with law firms regarding equity and inclusion issues.

Ms. Moss is active in many professional organizations and recently served on the Executive Committee of a large law firm marketing organization. When not practicing law or volunteering in the legal field, Ms. Moss volunteers with Operation Food Search, Habitat for Humanity, and TrailNet. She is a sometimes cyclist, an avid reader, and novice knitter. She is also acts as an unofficial ambassador for the State of Maine and will gladly share her love for summers there.

She and her husband live in University City, Missouri, their daughter attends Mount Holyoke College and their son is about to graduate from Worcester Polytechnic Institute in Worcester, Massachusetts.

attorneys.name: Timothy Robert Muehleisen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Prior to forming Edelman & Muehleisen, LLC, Tim spent 5 years with Edelman, deRoode, Muehleisen and Alton, LLC concentrating his practice in a variety of personal injury and workers compensation matters, along with minor criminal and traffic matters. Before that he spent 3 years with Smith Amundsen, a multi-practice law firm based in Chicago, Illinois. While there, he handled matters in a variety of areas including labor and employment disputes, construction litigation, contract disputes, commercial litigation, premises liability, products liability, toxic torts and general insurance defense. Prior to his time at Smith Amundsen, Tim was a partner at the law firm of Moser & Marsalek, PC in St. Louis. While there, he concentrated his practice in defending personal injury lawsuits that were filed against his clients across the country.

After 12 years spent mostly defending lawsuits, Tim decided that it was time to take that knowledge and skill set and begin practicing on the plaintiff side. During his career, Tim has taken cases to conclusion through trial of settlement on behalf of individuals, corporations, and small businesses. In addition to his trial work, Tim has also handled more than seventy-five mediations/arbitrations and has been very successful with disposing of matters prior to trial, obtaining favorable decisions on Motions for Summary Judgment and Motions to Dismiss in both State and Federal Court.

In 2011, Missouri Lawyers Weekly honored Tim as one of its 2011 Up & Coming Lawyers. The award honors attorneys under the age of 40. The recipient epitomizes excellence in the legal community and is identified as a leader in the community-at-large. In addition, Tim was also selected for inclusion in Missouri & Kansas Super Lawyers as a Rising Star for 2011 and 2013, which recognizes attorneys under the age of 40 that have attained a high-degree of peer recognition and professional achievement.

In his community, Timothy volunteers with Habitat for Humanity and is the founder and head coach of the Jr. Cougar Middle School football program for the Affton School District in St. Louis. He is also a board member of the Greek Literary Association for Kappa Sigma Fraternity (Beta-Gamma Chapter at the University of Missouri-Columbia). Timothy is licensed to practice in the states of Missouri and Illinois, as well as, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri and the United States Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit.

Areas of Practice:

Personal Injury matters including (but not limited to) the following: Motor Vehicle and Motorcycle Accidents, Tractor-Trailer Accidents, Bus Accidents, Premises Liability Cases, Dog Bits, Workers Compensation and Wrongful Death Cases

Additional areas of practice: minor criminal and traffic matters, commercial/business litigation, labor and employment disputes, contract disputes and landlord/tenant disputes.

attorneys.name: Loretta K. Haggard
attorneys.practice_type: Private and Public Sector Labor Unions Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Loretta Haggard focuses on Public Sector, Labor Law, Labor Law, and Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Appeals. Loretta came to the Firm after clerking for United States District Judge Jean C. Hamilton. She was co-counsel with Sally Barker in the Independence National Education Association v. Independence School District case, in which the Missouri Supreme Court recognized a state constitutional right of collective bargaining for public employees. Loretta co-authored Federal and State Law Governing Public Employees, 2008, Missouri Bar (and earlier editions); authored a law review article on accommodating mental disabilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act; and co-authored an article on the union's duties concerning coworker complaints of sexual harassment. She received the Missouri Lawyer’s Weekly Influential Appellate Attorney Award in 2022 and the Missouri Women's Justice Award for Litigation Practitioner in 2014, she previously Co-Chaired the Education Law Committee of the Missouri Bar Association. She received her dual law/social work degree (J.D./M.S.W., Order of the Coif) from Washington University in 1993 and her A.B., summa cum laude, from the School of Public and International Affairs at Princeton University in 1986. She is admitted to the bar in Missouri and Illinois, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Missouri and the Southern District of Illinois.

attorneys.name: Roger Nail
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Roger has been litigating high stakes personal injury cases since the late 1990’s. Missouri Lawyers Weekly reports of the verdicts and settlements he has obtained have been among the highest in the State of Missouri. He started the Nail Law Firm so he could focus on representing those injured by the negligence or intentional acts of others.

Roger is a graduate of Westminster College. He also holds a Masters of Arts in Public Policy and received his law degree from the University of Missouri at Columbia. While in law school he was a member of the Board of Advocates, the Journal of Dispute Resolution, and was afforded the opportunity to study law abroad at King’s College, Cambridge University.

Following graduation Roger served as a felony prosecutor in the Circuit Attorney’s Office in St. Louis, Missouri where he represented the people of the State of Missouri against felony criminal defendants.

He then worked at the international law firm of Shook Hardy & Bacon, LLC. While at Shook Hardy Roger represented multinational companies and healthcare providers in the defense of product liability and professional malpractice cases. Through his experience there he gained an understanding of the way corporate defendants and insurance companies litigate and value personal injury claims.

For nine years Roger was a partner at the Law Firm of Goza & Honnold where his practice was limited to representing those injured. This is where Roger honed his skills for getting complicated medical information from people with no medical or legal training and finding hidden evidence, making sure it isn’t lost or destroyed. He believes that a thorough investigation carried out quickly (personally or through private investigators) is essential. This belief has led to astounding trial results for his clients.

Since 2005 Roger has been representing victims of catastrophic injury and wrongful death in cases involving medical malpractice, nursing home negligence, motor vehicle accidents and product and premises liability cases. Roger has also represented clients across the nation in various mass tort product liability cases involving defective medical devices and/or drugs.

Much of Roger’s success in trial is due to the time he takes to get to know his clients. The more he knows about the people he represents and the details of their case, the harder he fights for fair and just compensation. Knowing how to become invested in his cases and provide honest and tenacious representation for his clients is the very reason Roger receives awards and recognition from some of the legal community’s most respected organizations.

In 2011 Roger was awarded the prestigious Thomas J. Conway Young Trial Lawyer Award by the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association. The Conway Award is given each year to one lawyer who exemplifies two traits: 1) outstanding trial skills, and 2) the ability to be a fierce advocate and a good friend to opposing counsel at the same time.

The same year he was also recognized by Ingram’s Magazine by his inclusion in their “40 Under Forty” publication. He is regularly recognized by the Kansas City Business Journal as one of the “Best of the Bar” and has been repeatedly chosen as a “Super Lawyer” by Super Lawyers Magazine. He is a Fellow of the Bar for the KCMBA and a Fellow of the Missouri Bar Foundation.

Since 2012 Roger has been recognized as one of Super Lawyers’ Top 50 attorneys in Kansas City and one of the Top 100 attorneys in the States of Missouri and Kansas. Roger has also been recognized as one of the National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers and is a member of the National Association of Distinguished Counsel. View

Roger has served as President of the Civil Litigation Section of the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association (“KCMBA”) and has chaired the Tort Committee for the Missouri Bar Association. He is a former Chair of the KCMBA Tort Committee and currently sits on the Board of the KCMBA and Chairs that organization’s CLE Committee. He is currently the president of the Civil Litigation Division of the Missouri Bar Association. He is a frequent speaker and presenter at seminars and CLE presentations including moderating and presenting at the Missouri Bar’s annual “Winning Strategies in Medical Malpractice” seminar. He lives in the Kansas City area with his wife and two young sons.

attorneys.name: Brett Newberry
attorneys.practice_type: Health Law Lawyers in Columbia, MO
attorneys.bio:
Brett Newberry brings a range of experience in health law, family law, and estate planning to her practice. With an undergraduate degree in the health professions, Brett possesses an uncommon blend of legal and medical knowledge that gives her a unique edge in the world of personal injury.

When choosing a profession, it was important to Brett to find a role which combined her desire to help others with her intellectual interests. After taking an undergraduate property law course taught by a law professor, it became clear that going to law school and becoming a lawyer was the perfect fit. When the time came to choose a practice area, personal injury was an obvious choice because it allowed Brett to combine her passions for healthcare, law, and advocacy all in one.

In her legal practice, Brett is a nuanced and strategic negotiator who is protective of her clients and their interests. Her broad range of experience in both the courtroom and alternative dispute resolution techniques allows her to customize her approach to each client’s unique case.

In her client relationships, Brett has gained a reputation as an empathetic, diligent, and hard-working attorney who fights for each client just as fiercely as she would fight for herself. One of the most rewarding parts of Brett’s work is the opportunity it provides to reduce the burdens her clients carry while they navigate some of the most difficult periods of their lives.

In her free time, Brett enjoys taking dance classes, reading, and going on bike rides with her family.

attorneys.name: Tim Nickless
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Hillsboro, MO
attorneys.bio:
Tim Nickless was born in St. Louis in 1986 and raised in Pevely, Missouri. Tim attended school at Herculaneum where he graduated Valedictorian of his class in 2004. Tim then attended the University of Missouri - Columbia where he studied business management.

While attending college at the University of Missouri, Tim was an active member of Chi Alpha Campus ministries where he took on leadership roles and held small group bible studies. Tim graduated in December 2007 with a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration. After graduating from Mizzou, Tim attended law school at the St. Louis University School of Law and was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 2013. Besides being admitted to the Missouri Bar, Tim is also licensed to practice in the US Federal District Courts in the Eastern District of Missouri.

Tim joined the Schnaare Law firm in August of 2016 and quickly made his presence known with his strong legal research and writing skills in assisting with complex litigation matters including will contests and land partition suits. In the time that Tim has been a part of this firm, his primary areas of practice has become Real Estate, Personal Injury, Family Law and Landlord-Tenant. Tim has a desire to continue to serve his hometown and surrounding areas in Jefferson County. Tim has a strong sense of community and networking within the Jefferson County region.

Tim now lives in Pacific, Missouri just inside the Jefferson County border, along with his wife Rachel, children and dogs. Tim grew up in Jefferson County and is proud to raise his own family here as well. Tim met his wife through the Boy Scouts of America Venturing Program, a coed portion of Boy Scouts. Tim joined Venturing after he obtained the rank of Eagle Scout at the age of 14. Tim and his wife are adult advisors for Venture Crew 2720 based out of Beaumont Scout Reservation which focuses on equine activities. Tim is also a Trail Guide for the Greater St. Louis Area Council. Tim continues to enjoy serving the Scouts because it was such a positive influence on his life growing up and he hopes to share that with the younger generations.

Prior to joining the Schnaare Law Firm, Tim practiced on his own for a couple years while pursuing another passion, one for the outdoors while working at Bass Pro Shops. Tim is a big advocate for 2nd amendment rights and conservation efforts. Any free time that Tim has is usually spent with his family or enjoying the outdoors, either hunting or fishing.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Tim Nickless was born in St. Louis in 1986 and raised in Pevely, Missouri. Tim attended school at Herculaneum where he graduated Valedictorian of his class in 2004. Tim then attended the University of Missouri - Columbia where he studied business management.

While attending college at the University of Missouri, Tim was an active member of Chi Alpha Campus ministries where he took on leadership roles and held small group bible studies. Tim graduated in December 2007 with a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration. After graduating from Mizzou, Tim attended law school at the St. Louis University School of Law and was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 2013. Besides being admitted to the Missouri Bar, Tim is also licensed to practice in the US Federal District Courts in the Eastern District of Missouri.

Tim joined the Schnaare Law firm in August of 2016 and quickly made his presence known with his strong legal research and writing skills in assisting with complex litigation matters including will contests and land partition suits. In the time that Tim has been a part of this firm, his primary areas of practice has become Real Estate, Personal Injury, Family Law and Landlord-Tenant. Tim has a desire to continue to serve his hometown and surrounding areas in Jefferson County. Tim has a strong sense of community and networking within the Jefferson County region.

Tim now lives in Pacific, Missouri just inside the Jefferson County border, along with his wife Rachel, children and dogs. Tim grew up in Jefferson County and is proud to raise his own family here as well. Tim met his wife through the Boy Scouts of America Venturing Program, a coed portion of Boy Scouts. Tim joined Venturing after he obtained the rank of Eagle Scout at the age of 14. Tim and his wife are adult advisors for Venture Crew 2720 based out of Beaumont Scout Reservation which focuses on equine activities. Tim is also a Trail Guide for the Greater St. Louis Area Council. Tim continues to enjoy serving the Scouts because it was such a positive influence on his life growing up and he hopes to share that with the younger generations.

Prior to joining the Schnaare Law Firm, Tim practiced on his own for a couple years while pursuing another passion, one for the outdoors while working at Bass Pro Shops. Tim is a big advocate for 2nd amendment rights and conservation efforts. Any free time that Tim has is usually spent with his family or enjoying the outdoors, either hunting or fishing.

attorneys.name: Ross C. Nigro Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Driving Under the Influence / Driving While Intoxicated Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
One of Kansas City’s most respected criminal defense attorneys, ROSS C. NIGRO, JR., has earned a reputation for providing high quality, aggressive legal representation. He has earned this reputation by providing his clients with the highest standards of diligence, knowledge and professional advice and by protecting his clients’ constitutional rights. Ross C. Nigro, Jr., is an attorney committed to providing excellence in defending his clients’ rights and ensuring positive results. Mr. Nigro treats his clients with respect and consideration. He is known for his strong work ethics, honesty, integrity, negotiating skills, and legal competency.

Ross C. Nigro, Jr., graduated from the University of Kansas with bachelor’s degrees in Political Science and History. Mr. Nigro obtained his Juris Doctorate from the University of Missouri, Kansas City - School of Law. Upon graduating from law school, Mr. Nigro worked as a law clerk with the Sixteenth Judicial Circuit of Missouri in Jackson County, Missouri. Mr. Nigro then went on to work as an Assistant Jackson County Counselor handling county prosecutions and civil rights violations. Since 1997, Mr. Nigro has been in private practice, where he has concentrated his practice in the criminal defense field. Mr. Nigro has over ten years of prosecuting experience.

Mr. Nigro is the Raytown Prosecuting Attorney, a position he has held since 2001. Mr. Nigro is also Raymore Municipal Judge and has held that position since 2015. Mr. Nigro served two terms as President of the Missouri Municipal and Associate Circuit Prosecutor’s Association. Mr. Nigro has served on the University of Missouri, Kansas City School of Law Alumni Board since 2006.

Mr. Nigro has received numerous awards and citations. Mr. Nigro has had a AV Preeminent Rating from Martindale-Hubbard since 2011. Mr. Nigro has been a member of the National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers since 2014. Mr. Nigro has been listed on Who’s Who of Legal Professionals since 2006. Mr. Nigro is listed as one of the top 20 criminal defense lawyers by Expertise. Nigro Law Firm has been awarded as one of the 10 best law firms by the American Institute of DUI/DWI attorneys.

attorneys.name: Parker Nocita
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accident Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Parker Nocita knew at an early age that he wanted to pursue a career in law when he began noticing the omnipresence of legal systems in everything from filmmaking to government. He was also inspired by his grandmother, a trailblazing U.S. Attorney who served in two federal districts.

After graduating from the University of Kansas and earning his law degree from the UMKC School of Law, Parker began his legal career clerking for a plaintiff’s personal injury firm, where he discovered a passion for advocating for individuals. Following a short stint in family law, he returned to personal injury work where he finds purpose in helping injured clients recover financially and emotionally.

Parker takes a client-first approach, valuing empathy, clear communication, and efficiency. Having experienced the challenges of an accident himself, he understands the frustrations clients face and works hard to enlighten clients and to make the process as smooth as possible.

A native of Overland Park, Kansas, Parker lives in the North Kansas City area with his two orange cats, Gilgamesh and Archie. Outside of work, he enjoys camping, music, writing, and going to the movie theater every chance he can get. He is active in the KCMBA, the St. Joseph Bar Association, and volunteers with Johnson County Parks and Recreation.

attorneys.name: Daniel Nolan
attorneys.practice_type: Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Dan Nolan forcefully advocates on behalf of clients at every stage of the criminal justice process, zealously representing those involved in select civil actions, as well. Focusing his attention first and foremost on the needs of clients, Mr. Nolan thoroughly evaluates, communicates, and fights for the most advantageous outcome to an unparalleled degree. With years of experience in a range of practice from impaired driving and their serious administrative consequences to serious felony cases, Mr. Nolan is an integral member of our legal team.

Specifically, Mr. Nolan is well-versed in the rules and regulations governing commercial and non-commercial driver licensing, including Driving While Intoxicated (DWI) and Driving Under the Influence (DUI) law; driver's license suspensions, revocations, denials, and cancellations; commercial disqualifications; limited and restricted driving privileges; and reinstatements, including reinstating drivers with 5-year, 10-year, and lifetime denials and disqualifications.

Mr. Nolan received both his undergraduate degree and law degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia. He is licensed to practice law in the states of Missouri and Illinois, as well as the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri, United States District Court for the Western District of Missouri, and United States District Court for the Southern District of Illinois.

attorneys.name: Robert G. Norfleet
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Robert's professional mission is to help folks that have been injured obtain the compensation they need and help make our communities safer by holding medical providers, drivers, and property owners responsible for violating safety rules and standards.

Robert Norfleet has fought against the insurance companies that defend doctors, hospitals, and nursing homes that endanger the health and safety of their patients. Robert also represents victims of catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death, including those that have been severely injured by negligent and reckless drivers, dangerous conditions of property, inadequate security, and defective products.

Unfortunately, the health care industry does a very poor job of enforcing the patient safety rules and often put profits over safety (link). In fact, very few health care providers ever face any discipline by state licensing boards, despite being sued multiple times for violating medical standards of care. Lawsuits are the only deterrent that gets the attention of the health care industry and helps improve patient safety. Each day Robert works to help make the health care industry safer for all of us by enforcing patient safety standards and holding health care providers accountable for violating these rules.

Robert has consistently been recognized as one of the top trial lawyers in the Midwest representing victims of negligence. He has been named a Super Lawyer for both Missouri and Kansas by Super Lawyers Magazine every year since 2015 (an honor given to more than 2.5% of attorneys in each state). The National Trial Lawyers recently named Robert to their list of Top 100 trial lawyers and their Top 25 list of Medical Malpractice Lawyers.

Every year Robert consistently obtains some of the largest verdicts and settlements for his clients in medical malpractice and catastrophic personal injury. He currently holds the record for the largest automobile accident jury verdict in Platte County in the last 8 years and the largest motorcycle accident jury verdict in Kansas City in the last 10 years.

Robert has extensive experience litigating cases involving brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, failed back surgeries, surgical injuries, orthopedic injuries, epidural hematomas, failure to diagnose cancer, failure to diagnose pulmonary embolism, failure to diagnose or treat infections resulting in sepsis or loss of limbs, failure to diagnose heart attack, stroke, bowel obstruction, failure to diagnose or treat fractures, injuries caused by improper IV drug administration, and compounding pharmacy negligence.

Unlike the lawyers hired by the insurance companies, who have no choice but to represent their insureds, Robert's practice allows him to choose the people he represents and the cases he wants to pursue. Robert will devote countless hours to each potential case, thoroughly reviewing the medical records, researching the issues in the case, and consulting with nationally renowned experts in the relevant fields. Robert believes in treating every client like family. Those clients whom he represents will receive thorough and meticulous attention to detail, zealous advocacy, and a personalized approach to their case.

If you or a loved one has been harmed by the negligence or carelessness of another, please give Robert a call today for a FREE CASE EVALUATION.

attorneys.name: John (Jack) Norton

attorneys.bio:
Jack Norton was born in Kansas City, Missouri and has been a lifelong resident of Clay and Platte counties. Mr. Norton attended the University of Missouri-Columbia and graduated with a B.A. in History in 1974. Mr. Norton attended Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan where he graduated with distinction in 1978. Mr. Norton was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 1978 at which time he joined his father, William Harrison Norton, in the practice of law at Norton & Pollard, P.C., which later became Norton, Pollard & Norton P.C., and eventually Norton & Norfleet, P.C.

In his first 10 years of practice Mr. Norton had a general practice including domestic relations, traffic law, personal injury and numerous civil matters. attorneys.name: Andrew A. O'Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Mesothelioma and Asbestos Law Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
For the past 20 years, Andrew has concentrated his practice on mesothelioma and asbestos law. A native of Dublin, Ireland, Andrew graduated from University College Dublin Law School in 1986, and worked with the firm of Gaffney & Halligan for four years. Then, after moving to the United States and graduating from the Saint Louis University School of Law, Andrew founded the O’Brien Law Firm to commit all of his energy and resources to fighting to gain compensation for victims of asbestos diseases.

As a licensed asbestos attorney in Missouri, Illinois and the Republic of Ireland, he has successfully tried numerous cases to verdict. In 2001, the Missouri Bar Foundation cited Andrew O’Brien for “outstanding trial work” and presented him with the prestigious Lon O. Hocker Award, an award given annually by the Missouri Bar Foundation to young lawyers who have demonstrated unusual proficiency in the art of trial advocacy.

Andrew has also served on the Judicial Commission for the 22nd Judicial Circuit for the city of St. Louis, testified in front of both the House and the Senate and currently serves on the board of governors for the Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys (MATA).

In his spare time, Andrew is an active part of the Irish music community in St. Louis and accomplished Irish violin player. He and his wife, Lori, have two daughters and a son.
