attorneys.name: Ezinne Grace Okorocha Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Facing divorce or family law matters can be a very emotional process. For this reason, it is important to have hope, and having dedicated representation that understands what you are going through can make all of the difference. Ezinne "Grace" Okorocha is an Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm, PC and is ready to help and assist clients in and around Jackson County, Missouri from the firm's Kansas City family law office.

Grace earned her Masters in U.S. Law (LLM) from the University of Houston Law Center in May of 2020. Before this, she attended the Nigerian Law School in Lagos in 2018 where she became a Barrister & Solicitor of the Supreme Court. Before studying to become a lawyer, Grace obtained a Master's Degree in Management and Human Resource Management from the University of Phoenix. She also has a Bachelor of Law degree that she earned in 2005 from Abia State University in Nigeria. Grace is currently licensed and ready to assist clients in the State of Missouri.

Before joining the Kansas City family lawyers at Stange Law Firm, PC, Grace gained legal experience interning for the Travis County Attorney's Office in the Domestic Family Violence Division. In this role she would regularly attend team meetings and would follow court proceedings online. She also utilized pending cases to gain valuable legal research experience. Grace also spent time as an intern for the Harris County District Attorney's Office in the Misdemeanor Division where she spent time contacting victims of crimes for restitution, injury and punishment, performing discovery, preparing for trial and attended court with a supervising attorney. Grace has a high attention to detail and will work hard to ensure that your rights are protected throughout the duration of your family law matter.

Outside of her legal practice, Grace enjoys cooking and experimenting with new recipes. She also loves to travel and encounter new places.

attorneys.name: James G. Onder
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Webster Groves, MO
attorneys.bio:
James G. Onder is founder of OnderLaw, a preeminent personal injury and mass tort litigation firm with offices in St. Louis, Missouri; Nashville, Tennessee; and Newport Beach, California. Mr. Onder takes great pride in changing the way corporations do business, the firm’s motto being, we not only take on cases, we take on causes. His accomplished team includes 30 attorneys and over 150 dedicated staff members. In addition to achieving more than $5 billion in settlements and verdicts representing plaintiffs’ interests, Mr. Onder negotiated a groundbreaking $8.9 billion agreement with Johnson & Johnson on behalf of current and future talc-related cancer victims.

Mr. Onder is a founder of talcum powder-related ovarian cancer litigation, having filed the second case in the nation and the first in the State of Missouri in 2014. OnderLaw, currently represents over 20,000 women who have suffered talc-related cancers and their survivors in what is believed to be the largest such docket in the country. He is also a founder of mini-blind-related death and injury litigation. His work has resulted in countless young lives saved because of changes he forced in miniblind design.

In 2016, OnderLaw, was recognized for achieving the first, second, and third largest verdicts in the state of Missouri, and the third-highest verdict in 2017. Representative firm achievements include but are not limited to: leading Missouri litigation by representing more than 24,000 plaintiffs in the Bayer-Monsanto glyphosate-related non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma coordinated Missouri litigation; serving as primary or local counsel for more than 20,000 talc-related cancer cases and leading six trial teams that obtained verdicts in excess of $300 million; serving as national co-chair of the Plaintiffs’ Law and Briefing Committee, on Discovery, Science and Expert Committees for both the MDL and JCCP, and as national co-lead counsel in the MDL in Yasmin, Yaz, and Ocella birth control cases; serving on Science and Expert Committees in gadolinium-based contrast agent cases; serving as local and national coordinating council in a certified mass action representing corn producers against Syngenta; serving on MDL Science, Expert, and Daubert and JCCP Plaintiffs’ Steering Committee in Zoloft-related birth defects cases; serving on Plaintiff’s Executive Committee in Zantac California JCCP; serving on Plaintiff’s Steering Committee in Truvada California JCCP; serving as national co-lead counsel in Tasigna product liability MDL; serving on the Leadership Committee for Syngenta Paraquat California JCCP; and serving on the Bankruptcy Tort Claims Committee in both the Imerys Talc America, Inc. and LTL (“J&J”) bankruptcies.

James G. Onder has earned a Martindale-Hubbell AV peer review rating; is a member of the board of governors of the Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys; achieved Nine Figure Litigator and Super Lawyers designations; is a member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, The American Society of Legal Advocates, and National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Trial Lawyers; and has received the National Litigator Award, among numerous additional recognitions.

attorneys.name: Kayla Onder
attorneys.practice_type: Sexual Abuse & Assault Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Kayla Ferrel joined OnderLaw in 2014; but before joining the firm, she was known nationally for competing in the television series, America’s Next Top Model, where she was then invited back as a fan favorite to the Reunion Series. She became well known for sharing her survivor’s story with the world. Impassioned with a desire to make a difference, Kayla returned to law school, passed the Bar exam, and is now empowered to help the victims of sexual abuse.

As with survivors, we are better in numbers. Appreciating that reality, Kayla has spent over a decade forging national relationships and has solidified partnerships with Sex Abuse litigators across the country. With these partnerships, the OnderLaw team has represented survivors of sexual abuse across the country, holding abusers and enabling institutions legally accountable and delivering nearly one billion dollars in recovery.

Kayla currently leads the firm’s Sexual Abuse practice, advocating on behalf of survivors across the country. Teaming with both survivors that are ready to be vocal advocates, as well as those who need their stories to remain highly confidential, Kayla is truly a confidant to all. Together, we are making a difference.

attorneys.name: Jack Paisley
attorneys.practice_type: Pre-Litigation Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Jack Paisley was immersed in the legal world from an early age. With a judge for a father and a court reporter for a mother, he has always been comfortable in the courtroom. It was the desire to stand up for those facing injustice that ultimately led him to pursue a career in law.

Before joining the firm, Jack served as a public defender, where he gained extensive trial experience and developed a reputation for fearless advocacy. One of his most memorable victories involved successfully defending a wheelchair-bound client wrongfully accused of theft, a case that reaffirmed his commitment to standing up for those without a voice.

Jack approaches every case as if he’s representing a close friend or family member. He builds trust with clients by listening closely and communicating with compassion and clarity. He also values maintaining respectful, professional relationships with opposing counsel to keep negotiations constructive and focused on fair outcomes.

Originally from Taylorville, Illinois, Jack attended Arizona State University before earning his law degree from Saint Louis University. Outside of work, he enjoys playing guitar, listening to music, and spending time with friends and family.

attorneys.name: John Parisi
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
I began as an associate with Shamberg, Johnson & Bergman in 1989, and became a partner in 1994. I practice in the areas of personal injury, medical malpractice, products liability, false claims act, (qui tam) cases, nursing home abuse cases and environmental law.

Prior to obtaining my law degree in 1989, I was a professional archaeologist for ten years. I conducted numerous archaeological excavations of historic Euro-American and prehistoric Indian Sites, primarily in Missouri and Kansas and participated in an archaeological survey for prehistoric sites in the Republic of Egypt in the Western Sahara Desert. As a lawyer, I have utilized the research and practical skills I developed as an archaeologist to the benefit of my clients.

Although I enjoyed being an archeologist, I became a lawyer primarily so that I could help real people whose problems exist in the present, rather than focusing on the lives of those people who lived in the past. Since becoming a lawyer I have dedicated my practice to representing seriously injured clients. I have been privileged to handle a wide variety of cases during my legal career. I have successfully brought to conclusion complex cases both for individual clients and as class actions. I have obtained substantial recoveries for my clients in a wide variety of cases, including defective drugs, defective products, negligent health care, and environmental contamination. I have also represented a number of whistleblowers that have recovered millions of dollars to the United States Treasury.

I am also committed to improving the legal community. I believe that lawyers have a duty not only to their clients, but also to the civil justice system and their community. I currently serve on a number of bar association committees and leadership positions. I served as a commissioner for eight years and was elected Chairman the last year for the Kansas Lawyers Fund for Client Protection (LFCP or The Fund). I am a Past President of the Kansas Association for Justice.

I am married to Ellen Suzanne Goldman, also a lawyer, and I have two children, Laura and Julie. My interests outside the law include prehistoric North American archeology, music, traveling and bicycling.

attorneys.name: Christopher T. Patterson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Platte City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Chris Patterson has been a private practice attorney since 1980. He has extensive experience in several areas of the law, but presently practices primarily in Divorce and Custody, Traffic/Driving While Intoxicated, Mediation, Criminal Law, Juvenile Law, and Wills and Trusts.

Chris graduated from the University of Missouri-Columbia in 1976 with a Bachelor of Journalism degree. He received his law degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia School of Law in 1980. Since then, he has practiced primarily in the Platte, Clay and Jackson County courts, where he is a well-respected member of the legal community. He is regularly appointed by judges as a Guardian ad Litem, representing the interests of children. In 1998, and again in 2010, he was one of three attorneys submitted to the Governor of Missouri for consideration for a judicial appointment in Platte County. Chris values his reputation as an honest, hard working, reasonable and effective attorney.

Volunteer interests have kept Chris connected with the pulse of the community. He has been an active Young Life leader and trainer since 1982 and received the Young Life National Volunteer Leader Award of Excellence in 2012. Young Life is an ecumenical Christian organization whose primary focus is youth. Chris works with high school students, as well as the training of leaders and staff, both locally and nationally. He has authored a book, "The Adventure," which is published by Young Life. Chris is an active member of 12 Apostles Catholic Parish in Platte City, Missouri.

Chris has received the Excellence in Education Award from the KCI/Northland Regional Chamber of Commerce for his service to education. He is also a member of the Platte County R-III High School Pirate Hall of Fame and a member of the Board of Directors of the Platte County Education Foundation. Chris has been considered for multiple judicial panels and has argued and won a Mechanic's Lien case before the Missouri Supreme Court - Commercial Openings, Inc. v. Mathews, 819 S.W.2d 347 (Mo. banc 1991).

attorneys.name: Joseph J. Piatchek
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Springfield, MO
attorneys.bio:
Brief Autobiography of

Joseph J. Piatchek, Attorney and Counselor at Law

I was born in Springfield, Missouri and I have spent most of my life here in the Ozarks. I attended elementary, middle school, and high school in Springfield. I attended college (undergraduate and Law School) at the University of Missouri - Columbia.

After graduating with a degree in Psychology, I returned to Springfield to work at Lakeland Regional Hospital. I worked with adolescents who were suffering with various forms of mental illness, abuse, and neglect. I also worked at The Burrell Center as a social worker/case manager for senior adults with persistent and acute mental illness. During this time, I first began exploring my role as a counselor to others. This is also when I was first exposed to the legal field, regularly dealing with many government agencies, courts, police, and occasionally attending guardianship hearings. I eventually decided to attend law school.

After graduating with my law degree, and passing the Missouri Bar Exam, I returned to my hometown of Springfield and worked for a personal injury firm. I then decided to hang out a shingle and begin my own law practice. The rest is history.

Today, I am the Managing Attorney at The Piatchek Law Firm, LLC. I am also a certified mediator, in addition to being a Member of The Missouri Bar, and The American Bar Association, including the ABA Business Law Section. I am also a Notary Public, and provide mobile notary, witnessing, and loan closing services throughout Missouri.

In addition, I regularly donate my time and services to local churches and non-profit agencies, and regularly provide pro-bono services through The Piatchek Law Firm, LLC.

In the past, I have volunteered time for Legal Services of Southern Missouri, a non-profit agency providing free or low cost legal services to those who could not otherwise afford a private attorney.

Currently, I live in Springfield with my wonderful wife, and best friend, Tracy Piatchek. Tracy is an elementary school teacher for the Springfield Public School system. In my spare time, I enjoy playing basketball, golf, exercising, cooking, and spending time with Tracy.

attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Andy Pichler was born and raised in St. Louis, Missouri. Andy attended Westminster College and graduated with a degree in Sports Management and Marketing in 2014. He then attended St. Louis University School of Law and earned his law degree in 2017. After law school and passing the Missouri Bar, Andy began his legal career practicing Family Law. The five years he spent litigating domestic cases gave him a look at some of the hardships clients are facing when they need an attorney. Helping his clients navigate through the emotional and financial stresses of divorce or child custody matters gave him an understanding and appreciation for what it takes to make a positive difference in a client's life. His experience handling such hardships allows Andy to relate to and effectively communicate with clients who are physically injured. He has the experience and the empathy to better understand and represent the voice of his clients, whose injuries are leaving them faced with many physical, emotional and financial uncertainties. Andy has spent the last three years representing injured clients both in civil and workers' compensation matters. When Andy is not at the office, he enjoys spending time with his friends and family, especially his wife and daughter. He also enjoys playing golf and rooting for the St. Louis Cardinals and Blues, Tennessee Titans and Notre Dame Figthting Irish.

attorneys.name: Cheryl Pilate
attorneys.firm_name: Morgan Pilate LLC Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Justice Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Cheryl has dedicated her law practice to the vigorous protection of individual rights, including the representation of criminal defendants and those who have suffered a violation of their constitutional rights. She believes that when a citizen faces criminal charges, there is nothing more important than having a strong, dedicated and effective advocate at his or her side.

Cheryl is perhaps best known for her work on innocence cases, including obtaining the exoneration and release of persons convicted of crimes they did not commit. Cheryl currently serves as vice president of the Midwest Innocence Project, an organization that advocates for and seeks the release of the wrongfully convicted.

Cheryl's diverse practice includes not only the zealous representation of criminal defendants, but also the representation of individuals who have suffered illegal discrimination or other violations of their constitutionally protected rights. She has successfully sued on behalf of the wrongfully convicted, obtaining rightful compensation for years of lost liberty.

Cheryl has represented criminal defendants in the most serious and complex of criminal cases, running the gamut from first-degree and capital murder to drug and white collar cases including alleged fraud, tax evasion and Internet solicitation or pornography crimes.

Cheryl is a 1976 graduate of the University of Michigan, where she served as co-editor-in-chief of the Michigan Daily. For several years after graduation, she worked as a newspaper reporter, including five years at the Wichita Eagle & Beacon. She obtained a Master's in social work from the University of Kansas in 1983 and her law degree from the University of Kansas School of Law in 1990. Cheryl graduated with honors, then spent two years serving as a law clerk for the Honorable John R. Gibson of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

Cheryl worked for 15 years at the firm of Wyrsch, Hobbs & Mirakian. She became a shareholder at Wyrsch Hobbs in 1992 and remained there until opening her own practice with Melanie Morgan. In June 2007, Melanie and Cheryl founded Morgan Pilate LLC.

Cheryl has successfully represented numerous defendants facing capital charges as well as clients on death row. Her work on behalf of the wrongfully convicted included the successful representation of Ellen Reasonover, a Missouri woman who served more than 16 years in prison for a murder she did not commit. After working, along with others, to obtain Ms. Reasonover's release, Cheryl led a team of lawyers in obtaining civil damages for Ms. Reasonover to compensate her for the years of lost liberty.

Cheryl also represented in a civil lawsuit two other men who were wrongfully convicted, Dennis Fritz and Ron Williamson. Their stories are recounted in John Grisham's book, the Innocent Man, and in Mr. Fritz's book, Journey Toward Justice.

Cheryl is a member of several professional organizations, including the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Kansas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the American Bar Association, and the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association. She is also a fellow of the American Bar Foundation and has been recognized as among the Top 50 Women Lawyers in Kansas and Missouri. Cheryl is also AV rated by Martindale Hubbell.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Cheryl has dedicated her law practice to the vigorous protection of individual rights, including the representation of criminal defendants and those who have suffered a violation of their constitutional rights. She believes that when a citizen faces criminal charges, there is nothing more important than having a strong, dedicated and effective advocate at his or her side.

Cheryl is perhaps best known for her work on innocence cases, including obtaining the exoneration and release of persons convicted of crimes they did not commit. Cheryl currently serves as vice president of the Midwest Innocence Project, an organization that advocates for and seeks the release of the wrongfully convicted.

Cheryl's diverse practice includes not only the zealous representation of criminal defendants, but also the representation of individuals who have suffered illegal discrimination or other violations of their constitutionally protected rights. She has successfully sued on behalf of the wrongfully convicted, obtaining rightful compensation for years of lost liberty.

Cheryl has represented criminal defendants in the most serious and complex of criminal cases, running the gamut from first-degree and capital murder to drug and white collar cases including alleged fraud, tax evasion and Internet solicitation or pornography crimes.

Cheryl is a 1976 graduate of the University of Michigan, where she served as co-editor-in-chief of the Michigan Daily. For several years after graduation, she worked as a newspaper reporter, including five years at the Wichita Eagle & Beacon. She obtained a Master's in social work from the University of Kansas in 1983 and her law degree from the University of Kansas School of Law in 1990. Cheryl graduated with honors, then spent two years serving as a law clerk for the Honorable John R. Gibson of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.

Cheryl worked for 15 years at the firm of Wyrsch, Hobbs & Mirakian. She became a shareholder at Wyrsch Hobbs in 1992 and remained there until opening her own practice with Melanie Morgan. In June 2007, Melanie and Cheryl founded Morgan Pilate LLC.

Cheryl has successfully represented numerous defendants facing capital charges as well as clients on death row. Her work on behalf of the wrongfully convicted included the successful representation of Ellen Reasonover, a Missouri woman who served more than 16 years in prison for a murder she did not commit. After working, along with others, to obtain Ms. Reasonover's release, Cheryl led a team of lawyers in obtaining civil damages for Ms. Reasonover to compensate her for the years of lost liberty.

Cheryl also represented in a civil lawsuit two other men who were wrongfully convicted, Dennis Fritz and Ron Williamson. Their stories are recounted in John Grisham's book, the Innocent Man, and in Mr. Fritz's book, Journey Toward Justice.

Cheryl is a member of several professional organizations, including the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Kansas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the American Bar Association, and the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association. She is also a fellow of the American Bar Foundation and has been recognized as among the Top 50 Women Lawyers in Kansas and Missouri. Cheryl is also AV rated by Martindale Hubbell.

attorneys.name: Angela E. Pozzo
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Liability Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
MEDICAL & HEALTH CARE LITIGATION

Angela Pozzo is an associate in the Medical and Health Care Litigation group of Moser & Marsalek, P.C. She joined the firm in 2004. She focuses her practice on defending physicians, nurses, long term care facilities and other health care providers in medical negligence, ordinary negligence and wrongful death litigation. Ms. Pozzo also has experience defending medical device manufacturers.

Over the past five years, Ms. Pozzo has defended physicians, nurses, health care institutions, long term care facilities, and medical device manufacturers in all aspects of litigation, including second-chairing multiple medical negligence and wrongful death trials. In 2006, she tried her first medical negligence case and obtained a defense verdict for a local oncology practice against a claimed failure to timely diagnose lung cancer.

In 2001, Ms. Pozzo obtained a Bachelor's degree, summa cum laude, from Illinois State University with a double major in political science and communications. She received her law degree from Saint Louis University School of Law in 2004, along with Certificate in Health Law Studies. During law school, Ms. Pozzo completed an internship with the U.S. Attorney's office for the Southern District of Illinois where she presented to a state task force on nursing home fraud and abuse.

SELECTED CASES

Trinidy Noldon, by and through her next friend and mother, Vatisha Chester v. Saint Louis University, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri, 2008. Ms. Pozzo served as second chair counsel with Principal Phillip Willman in the successful defense of Saint Louis University in obstetrical negligence case that claimed the fourth largest defense verdict in Missouri in 2008 by Missouri Lawyer's Weekly.

Connie Parish v. Bond, M.D., and Kingshighway/New Halls Ferry Medical Services, LLC, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri, 2008. Ms. Pozzo served as second chair counsel with Principal Philip Willman in obtaining a unanimous defense verdict in favor of a local internist. Plaintiff alleged the defendant internist failed to appropriately manage her blood pressure causing her to suffer an intracerebral hemorrhage resulting in brain injury and left-sided neurologic deficits.

Hoff v. St. John's Mercy Medical Center, et al., St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri, 2007. Ms. Pozzo served as second chair counsel with Principal Philip Willman in obtaining a defense verdict for a local spine surgeon. Plaintiff, a trauma patient with a thoracic spine fracture and a seizure disorder, alleged a spine surgeon delayed surgery, resulting in his experiencing seizures and paralysis.

Marla Cohen v. Ballas Cancer Center, d/b/a St. Louis Cancer and Breast Institute, L.L.C., et al., St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri, 2006. Ms. Pozzo successfully defended St. Louis Cancer and Breast Institute against Plaintiff's claim that her lung cancer was not timely diagnosed.

PUBLICATIONS

Medlaw Update, DRI Newsletter case note, April 2009, reporting on the Missouri Supreme Court's holding in Janice Sides v. St. Anthony's Medical Center, et al., 258 S.W.3d 811, (Mo. banc 2008), that in a medical negligence case, plaintiff may proceed under a theory of res ipsa loquitur by offering testimony of medical experts that the injury would not have occurred in the absence of defendant's negligence.

A native of Palatine, Illinois, Stephanie attended the University of Missouri-Columbia where she graduated with dual degrees in English and classical humanities. Her work ethic resulted in her earning departmental honors in English, as well as an honors certificate from the university’s honors college.

Following her time at Mizzou, Stephanie obtained her law degree from Saint Louis University School of Law and utilized her writing skills as an Editor on the Journal of Health Law and Policy. In addition to earning her Juris Doctor, she also secured a Health Law certificate from the Saint Louis University Health Law program, which has continually been ranked as the top health law program in the nation, according to U.S. News & World Report. She gained practical legal experience outside of the classroom, assisting indigent clients at the Saint Louis University School of Law Elder Law Clinic.

Since joining OnderLaw, Stephanie has focused her practice on representing personal injury and products liability victims, including mass tort litigation on a national scale. Stephanie brings to bear her health law experience to mass tort litigation. Stephanie is licensed to practice in the states of Missouri and Illinois.

attorneys.name: John M. Reeves
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation & Appeals Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
John Reeves is an appellate specialist. After serving as an Assistant Missouri Attorney General for over six years, he entered private practice in 2015 and opened his own firm in 2019.

He has personally authored over 270 appellate briefs and has conducted oral arguments in all three districts of the Missouri Court of Appeals, the Missouri Supreme Court, and the federal Eighth Circuit. In addition, Mr. Reeves has personally authored both certiorari petitions and applications for extraordinary relief before the Supreme Court of the United States. Mr. Reeves has also written numerous dispositive motions in both federal and state court.

Mr. Reeves also provides consulting services to trial attorneys about preserving matters for appeal and drafting dispositive motions.

In October 2019, Mr. Reeves co-founded the Missouri Bar’s Appellate Practice Committee, the first statewide organization in Missouri devoted to furthering professional development for attorneys in appellate matters. He presently serves as the committee’s co-chair. In 2021, Mr. Reeves received the Outstanding Service Award from the Missouri Organization of Defense Lawyers for his amicus appellate briefing on MODL’s behalf. That same year, he also received the International Municipal Lawyers’ Association Amicus Service Award for an amicus brief he filed in support of a petition for a writ of certiorari in the Supreme Court of the United States.

attorneys.name: Adam Reynolds
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Adam is a Magna Cum Laude graduate of Truman State University and Washington University School of Law, where he also served on Law Review and received membership in the Order of the Coif. Adam joined O’Brien Law Firm in 2014 with the professional goal of seeking justice for clients whose personal health or loved ones’ lives have been needlessly endangered.

Utilizing his strong research and writing abilities, Adam helps to maximize client recoveries by responding to complex legal issues as part of the Firm’s motion practice in civil cases, by taking depositions, and by arguing motions in court. Adam has also helped spearhead the Firm’s growing workers’ compensation practice for occupational diseases due to toxic exposure in recent years, which has resulted in settlements and awards totaling millions of dollars in compensation. As part of this practice, Adam has handled numerous hearings in the Division of Workers’ Compensation and has written successful appellate briefs filed with the Missouri Labor and Industrial Relations Commission and the Missouri Court of Appeals.

Adam became interested in law after spending a summer in college working for a plaintiffs’ employment discrimination firm in Kansas City, MO. After his first year of law school, Adam wrote post-conviction motions and direct appeal briefs while conducting legal research projects for the Missouri State Public Defender’s Appellate Division in downtown St. Louis. With interests in history and travel, Adam now calls St. Louis home after growing up in Kansas City. Adam is a member of the American Association for Justice and the Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys.

attorneys.name: Craig W. Richards
attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Webster Groves, MO
attorneys.bio:
Class Actions, Consumer Protection, and Wrongful Repossession & Debt Collection.

Craig Richards received his undergraduate and master’s degrees in accounting from the University of Missouri Columbia before obtaining his Juris Doctorate from St. Louis University School of Law. Following law school, Craig worked as a law clerk for the Honorable Colleen Dolan at the Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District, where he gained valuable experience in an array of legal issues.

Since joining OnderLaw in 2018, Craig’s practice has focused primarily on consumer protection and class actions. Craig is licensed to practice in Missouri and currently resides in St. Louis.

Although most of Craig’s clients live in Missouri and are litigated in state and federal Missouri courts, he works with nation-wide class action litigation and regularly works on cases filed out-of-state, primarily in New York, Georgia, Indiana, Oklahoma, Kentucky, and Connecticut.

Craig is dedicated to helping his prospective clients and will give them an honest assessment of their potential claims or defenses at no cost. In fact, most of Craig’s clients never have to pay out-of-pocket fees. Unless he successfully handles your suit and can recover from the opposing party, he receives no compensation. Accordingly, clients can feel confident he is committed to effectively and efficiently resolving their case. In most cases, he gives his clients the opportunity to protect and vindicate their rights without having to commit any of their hard-earned money.

attorneys.name: Kevin C. Roberts
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Hillsboro, MO
attorneys.bio:
Kevin, a partner since 1987, graduated with a B.S. from South Dakota State University. He received his Law Degree from the University of Missouri in 1981. Kevin was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 1981 and the South Dakota Bar in 1983. He is also admitted to practice before all Federal Courts in Missouri, the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court.

Kevin began his legal career after graduation as a law clerk to the Honorable John K. Regan in the United States District Court in St. Louis. He worked for a short time at Brown, James & Rabbitt in St. Louis before moving his practice to Jefferson County where he partnered with former Missouri Governor Jay Nixon. Kevin has actively practiced in Jefferson County for the past 30 years trying numerous civil and criminal jury trials. Kevin focuses his practice on personal injury, wrongful death claims, mass torts and all types of litigation both civil and criminal.

Kevin is a member of the Missouri Bar, Jefferson County Bar, State Bar of South Dakota, American Bar Association, American Association for Justice, Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys and the National Association and Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys.

Kevin has previously served on the Board of Directors for Legal Services of Eastern Missouri and as Chairman of the Missouri Lottery Commission. He is past President of the Jefferson County Bar Association and Past President of the Hillsboro School Board, having served on that Board for 14 years. Kevin is currently serving as the Vice-Chairman of the Missouri State Fair Commission and remains active in many local boards and organizations.

attorneys.name: Matthew Robertson
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Financial Services Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Robertson advises and assists clients in a variety of civil litigation matters and at all stages in the process from client intake to jury verdict. Matthew’s practice focuses on consumer financial services and consumer credit and background information issues. With an unwavering commitment to justice and fairness, Matthew leads his clients through their legal battles. Matthew enjoys navigating complex legal problems and brings that energy into each case he takes on, ensuring clients, no matter where they have come from, have a clear and effective path toward their legal goals.

Matthew’s diligence, creative approach, and ability to navigate complex legal issues produces effective solutions to complicated matters. Matthew ensures that everyone, regardless of their background and socio-economic status, has access to quality legal representation by being the attorney they deserve to succeed in their legal battles in the courts or in arbitration.

Matthew earned his law degree from Washburn University School of Law with Dean’s Honors and earned his bachelor’s degree in political science from the University of Kansas. Matthew is admitted to practice in Kansas and Missouri and in the federal courts of Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, Colorado, the Western District of Wisconsin, and the Southern District of Indiana. He is a member of the National Association of Consumer Advocates.

Prior to law school Matt served in the U.S. Army, and is a veteran of Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation New Dawn. When not at the office, Matthew spends his time with his family and enjoys spending time outdoors.

attorneys.name: Burke D. Robinson
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Litigation: Business Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Companies in the construction industry rely on Burke Robinson for practical, results-oriented legal representation. Recognized by Best Lawyers as Lawyer of the Year for his work in construction law, Burke brings more than 20 years of focused industry experience to advising and advocating for commercial contractors, suppliers, condominium homeowners’ associations, developers, owners and sureties.

Litigation

Burke represents construction clients in the full range of disputes, including construction defect matters, payment and delay claims, and insurance coverage issues—often in cases involving 10 to 20 parties. He has successfully litigated numerous multimillion-dollar claims through arbitration and in state and federal courts. Burke has also foreclosed on millions of dollars’ worth of mechanics liens on commercial and pipeline properties. Since 2009, he has served as local counsel for Missouri and Kansas through National Lien and Bond, prosecuting liens for commercial contractors throughout both states.

Transactional Counsel

Burke drafts and negotiates contracts for general contractors, subcontractors and suppliers. His litigation background gives clients a strategic advantage; he uses lessons learned in the courtroom to craft contract terms designed to prevent disputes or withstand them when necessary.

Project Management

For developer clients, Burke provides comprehensive project oversight from inception to closeout. His work includes drafting, administering and enforcing construction and design contracts; monitoring construction progress to manage risk; preparing and processing pay applications; and handling lien waivers.

As a co-founder of Long & Robinson, LLC, Burke takes pride in delivering a true one-stop shop for the construction industry’s legal needs. He offers flexible alternatives to the traditional billable-hour model, including contingency and hybrid fee arrangements, and the firm’s ability to manage most litigation tasks in-house saves clients significant time, money and disruption.

Burke frequently speaks at continuing education seminars for engineers, architects and contractors, sharing practical insights on construction contracting, risk management, mechanics liens and alternative dispute resolution.

Outside the office, Burke enjoys an active lifestyle. He is an avid fly fisherman and enjoys international travel and snow skiing.

Reported Cases

attorneys.name: Amanda C. Robinson
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Amanda focuses her practice on real estate litigation and commercial cost recovery across the country. As part of her practice she exclusively developed an efficient and cost-effective program to successfully manage and resolve all aspects of third party subpoenas for both small businesses and large, Fortune 500 companies throughout the U.S. The program encompasses paper and e-discovery collection, review, and production, along with depositions and motion practice. Amanda has negotiated with thousands of parties in numerous jurisdictions to reach favorable and cost-effective resolutions for clients.

Amanda also has twelve years of experience handling complex global products liability cases, with an emphasis on overseeing discovery in multi-district litigations. This role pairs Amanda's e-discovery expertise with her expertise coordinating counsel across multiple jurisdictions to negotiate and resolve discovery issues. Amanda develops and implements creative, cost-effective approaches to address disputes and her tailored approach toward collection, review, and production of data is invaluable to ensure that clients are able to meet their discovery obligations efficiently and strategically.

Amanda has extensive pro bono experience, focusing on criminal, family law, and other general legal matters for the underprivileged in the Kansas City area. She represents juveniles and serves as a court-appointed Guardian ad Litem for children in Jackson County. She also volunteers for Legal Aid of Western Missouri's Warrant Relief Program and the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Foundation's Military Matters program. She has spoken at Continuing Legal Education programs focusing on pro bono representation and at various organizations related to new and creative ways to reach the underprivileged community.

In recognition of her pro bono efforts, Amanda has received the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association's Robert C. Welch Volunteer Attorney Project Award, Shook, Hardy & Bacon, LLP's William G. Zimmerman Pro Bono Award, and the Helping Hands Give Hope Award from the City Union Mission. Her dedication to pro bono work has also been recognized in Ingram's magazine, City Union Mission's The Light, Kansas City Rescue Mission's Connection, The Missouri Bar's Young Lawyer's e-newsletter, and on The Missouri Bar's Pro Bono Wall of Fame.

Amanda has been honored to serve on KCMBA's Pro Bono Task Force, the board of directors for the City Union Mission and Bessie's House, and on the Lee's Summit advisory board for the Truman Heartland Community Foundation.

Prior to joining Long & Robinson, LLC as a Partner, Amanda was employed by Shook, Hardy & Bacon, LLP from 2005-2017, most recently serving as Of Counsel. She represented business interests in the tobacco, pharmaceutical, and real estate industries.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Amanda focuses her practice on real estate litigation and commercial cost recovery across the country. As part of her practice she exclusively developed an efficient and cost-effective program to successfully manage and resolve all aspects of third party subpoenas for both small businesses and large, Fortune 500 companies throughout the U.S. The program encompasses paper and e-discovery collection, review, and production, along with depositions and motion practice. Amanda has negotiated with thousands of parties in numerous jurisdictions to reach favorable and cost-effective resolutions for clients.

Amanda also has twelve years of experience handling complex global products liability cases, with an emphasis on overseeing discovery in multi-district litigations. This role pairs Amanda's e-discovery expertise with her expertise coordinating counsel across multiple jurisdictions to negotiate and resolve discovery issues. Amanda develops and implements creative, cost-effective approaches to address disputes and her tailored approach toward collection, review, and production of data is invaluable to ensure that clients are able to meet their discovery obligations efficiently and strategically.

Amanda has extensive pro bono experience, focusing on criminal, family law, and other general legal matters for the underprivileged in the Kansas City area. She represents juveniles and serves as a court-appointed Guardian ad Litem for children in Jackson County. She also volunteers for Legal Aid of Western Missouri's Warrant Relief Program and the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Foundation's Military Matters program. She has spoken at Continuing Legal Education programs focusing on pro bono representation and at various organizations related to new and creative ways to reach the underprivileged community.

In recognition of her pro bono efforts, Amanda has received the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association's Robert C. Welch Volunteer Attorney Project Award, Shook, Hardy & Bacon, LLP's William G. Zimmerman Pro Bono Award, and the Helping Hands Give Hope Award from the City Union Mission. Her dedication to pro bono work has also been recognized in Ingram's magazine, City Union Mission's The Light, Kansas City Rescue Mission's Connection, The Missouri Bar's Young Lawyer's e-newsletter, and on The Missouri Bar's Pro Bono Wall of Fame.

Amanda has been honored to serve on KCMBA's Pro Bono Task Force, the board of directors for the City Union Mission and Bessie's House, and on the Lee's Summit advisory board for the Truman Heartland Community Foundation.

Prior to joining Long & Robinson, LLC as a Partner, Amanda was employed by Shook, Hardy & Bacon, LLP from 2005-2017, most recently serving as Of Counsel. She represented business interests in the tobacco, pharmaceutical, and real estate industries.

attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Protection Law Lawyers in Webster Groves, MO
attorneys.bio:
Jesse's practice is devoted primarily to consumer protection law. He is an avid litigator who believes in the importance of fighting for the people who can least afford to be cheated out of their hard-earned money by businesses with little or no consciences. Jesse has had many successful class actions against banks, credit unions and finance companies challenging their repossession practices. Through these class actions, Jesse has obtained over $50 million in debt forgiveness, cash payments, and credit report repair.

Jesse earned his bachelor's degrees in finance and accounting from Indiana University. He graduated magna cum laude from Southern Illinois University School of Law. Jesse is admitted to practice law in Missouri, Illinois, and the United States District Courts for the Eastern District of Missouri, Southern District of Illinois, Southern District of Indiana and the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals. Before joining the Onder Law Firm, Jesse was an attorney at a large law firm in the City of St. Louis specializing in business litigation.

Jesse is a member of the Bar Association of Metropolitan St. Louis and the American Bar Association.

attorneys.bio:

attorneys.practice_type: Product Liability Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Rachal Rojas is an attorney at TorHoerman Law who specializes in product liability and pharmaceutical litigation.

A Corpus Christi, TX native, Rachal moved cross-country to attend Columbia University in New York City and completed a bachelor’s degree in political science.

Before law school and after graduating from Columbia, she worked on both sides of civil litigation as a paralegal for a plaintiff’s asbestos law firm and a corporate defense firm.

Legal Career

Rachal graduated from the University of Houston Law Center in 2008 and began practicing shortly thereafter.

She worked at Matthews & Associates in Houston and New York for nine years, providing responsive representation to people injured by defective products, chemical exposure, dangerous drugs and medical devices, and more.

Rachal then worked for The Potts Law Firm, Johnson Law Group, and most recently D. Miller & Associates in Houston, TX until joining TorHoerman Law in 2023.

Rachal is an expert in product liability litigation, legal research, and is a welcome addition to the THL team.

attorneys.bio:
Nate Ross is a commercial litigator with over twenty years of experience. Nate’s legal practice is focused on disputes involving real estate, creditor’s rights, construction, general business and commercial matters. Nate enjoys watching sports, traveling and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: James Roswold
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Kansas Ctiy, MO
attorneys.bio:
James Roswold has been in practice since 1990. While still in law school, he obtained early litigation experience as a member of the Iowa Legal Clinic. During law school, he gained additional litigation experience clerking for a sole practitioner whose practice included personal injury.

James is a graduate of the University of Minnesota Carlson School of Management in Minneapolis, MN, graduating magna cum laude, and University of Iowa Law School in Iowa City, IA, receiving his law degree and graduating with distinction, and he is admitted to practice law in both State and Federal Courts in Missouri.

James started his legal career working for a defense litigation firm, where he handled personal injury, insurance, FELA, and asbestos cases. In a short time working for a defense firm, he gained an insight into "the other side's" preparation of a civil case, something that would become highly useful in his practice just three years later when he joined a law firm in Kansas City, MO and began his career of representing victims of injury accidents and medical negligence. There he was involved in all types of civil litigation, aggressively pursuing personal injury, medical malpractice, wrongful death, consumer fraud, charitable fundraising, property insurance and workers' compensation cases on behalf of injured victims. Two years later, he helped start a law firm in Kansas City, MO representing personal injury victims where he became a partner in 1999.

Fourteen years later, James decided he could best serve his clients by opening his own office for the practice of law in cases dealing with injured victims of personal injury, medical negligence, wrongful death, workers compensation, nursing home negligence, premises liability, product liability, and accident cases.

James welcomes all calls about any personal injury accident, work injury, nursing home injury, wrongful death, or injury from a doctor or hospital in the State of Missouri. He promises to give you a straightforward honest answer about every question you might ask.

Dedicated to Defending the Rights of Injured Victims

James takes pride in obtaining fair and just compensation for seriously injured people throughout Kansas & Missouri. Kansas City Accident Injury Attorneys has office locations in downtown Kansas City, MO; Overland Park, KS; Lee's Summit, MO; and Parkville, MO.

Having his own law firm, James is able to provide the most personalized and individualized attention to each and every one of his clients. In his office, every client is a very important person not a file. He treats his clients with the dignity and the respect that they deserve and expect from a professional. He prides himself on knowing the details of the cases he handles. He knows what happened last on the client's case when he receives a call because he was directly involved in the matter.

James is a prolific writer and Kansas City Accident Injury Attorneys publishes a monthly newsletter full of important legal news and fun facts. In addition to his newsletter, he produces and creates instructional videos and has created an ever-expanding educational video library that helps consumers learn about personal injury, medical malpractice and workers compensation law in Kansas & Missouri.

James has provided free legal services to brain injury and handicapped victims and others as a way of lending his knowledge and expertise to those who have been dealt unfortunate circumstances and are unable to afford legal services.

Biker, Rocker, Runner, Father

James loves riding his motorcycle, and is equally passionate about representing other bikers who’ve been injured in accidents. When he’s not at work or on his bike, James also plays guitar and sings in the KC Biker Band.

James is an endurance athlete and participates in triathlons and marathons. As part of giving back to the community, he raises money for charities and he and his family volunteer in connection with these events as well. He is also an active member of the YMCA and his family participates in their community activities as well.

James is married and has three children. He and his family regularly enjoy participating in sports and musical activities.

attorneys.name: Susan Nell Rowe
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Susan Nell Rowe has practiced employment law for over thirty years. She has handled jury trials and appeals, EEOC and MCHR charges and other matters. Her practice also includes counsel and advice, manager training, and the development of employee handbooks and policies. She has enforced non-compete agreements and has drafted employment contracts and severance agreements. She has investigated sexual harassment complaints and has helped managers and human resource professionals conduct harassment investigations. She has been selected as a mediator in over forty employment disputes. She has represented clients in many types of businesses, including healthcare, professional consulting, manufacturing, food service and hospitality, and personal services. She has also represented nonprofits and local governments. Her clients include executives and professionals, and she has counseled clients facing discipline and separation from employment. Prior to opening her own firm, Ms. Rowe practiced in a corporate law firm where she served on the management committee for many years. That experience gave her an understanding of employment law issues from the perspective of a business owner. By taking advantage of technology and keeping overhead low, she has been able to provide the expertise of an experienced employment attorney at a reasonable rate. Ms. Rowe believes in serving the St. Louis community, and she has been on the boards of several area non-profits, including Legal Services of Eastern Missouri, Inc., Deaconess Foundation, The Missouri Lawyers Trust Account Foundation and Eden Theological Seminary. Outside of her law practice, Ms. Rowe spends time studying horticulture and garden design. She is the mother of two adult children and she resides in the City of St. Louis.

Susan Nell Rowe has practiced employment law for over thirty years. She has handled jury trials and appeals, EEOC and MCHR charges and other matters. Her practice also includes counsel and advice, manager training, and the development of employee handbooks and policies. She has enforced non-compete agreements and has drafted employment contracts and severance agreements. She has investigated sexual harassment complaints and has helped managers and human resource professionals conduct harassment investigations. She has been selected as a mediator in over forty employment disputes. She has represented clients in many types of businesses, including healthcare, professional consulting, manufacturing, food service and hospitality, and personal services. She has also represented nonprofits and local governments. Her clients include executives and professionals, and she has counseled clients facing discipline and separation from employment. Prior to opening her own firm, Ms. Rowe practiced in a corporate law firm where she served on the management committee for many years. That experience gave her an understanding of employment law issues from the perspective of a business owner. By taking advantage of technology and keeping overhead low, she has been able to provide the expertise of an experienced employment attorney at a reasonable rate. Ms. Rowe believes in serving the St. Louis community, and she has been on the boards of several area non-profits, including Legal Services of Eastern Missouri, Inc., Deaconess Foundation, The Missouri Lawyers Trust Account Foundation and Eden Theological Seminary. Outside of her law practice, Ms. Rowe spends time studying horticulture and garden design. She is the mother of two adult children and she resides in the City of St. Louis.

attorneys.name: Ramie K. Ruble
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Hillsboro, MO
attorneys.bio:
Ramie Ruble joined Roberts, Wooten, and Zimmer in 2025. She received her J.D. from Saint Louis University School of Law in May 2025 and received a B.S. in Public Health with a concentration in Health Professions from The University of Alabama in 2018, graduating cum laude. Ramie is licensed to practice law in the state of Missouri. Ramie’s legal practice focuses on medical malpractice, personal injury, wrongful death, birth injury, workers’ compensation, and general civil litigation.

During her time in law school, Ramie focused on experiential learning, participating in Trial Advocacy I & II, as well as the Human Rights at Home Litigation Clinic. Ramie also served on the executive board of SLU’s Women’s Law Students Association, where she created and managed a peer mentorship program. Prior to law school, Ramie worked as a medical scribe in the Emergency Department and for orthopedic specialists.

In her free time, Ramie enjoys reading, sewing, crocheting, knitting, running, and baking.

attorneys.name: Samantha Sader
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Sammi is a senior associate attorney at Fisher Law LLC. As a Kansas City native, Sammi received her undergraduate degree from the University of Missouri-Kansas City. In 2012, Sammi moved to Miami, Florida for law school and graduated cum laude from the University of Miami School of Law. Since returning to Kansas City, Sammi has focused on family law litigation, adoption and appellate work. Sammi is licensed to practice law in both Missouri and Kansas.

Through a combination of experiences, Sammi has gained a thorough knowledge of the court system, the mediation process, and the intricacies of complex family law litigation. Sammi also serves as a guardian ad litem in both family law and adoption cases in the State of Missouri.

Sammi acts as Vice Chair for the Continuing Legal Education Committee of the Young Lawyer Section of the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association; presently sits on the Board of the Association of Family and Conciliation Courts; was formerly a member of the Young Lawyer's Section Counsel for the Missouri Bar; and previously participated in the National Family Law Trial Institute, KCMBA's Bar Leadership Academy, and Ross T. Roberts Trial Academy.

Additionally, Sammi was recently honored as a 2021 Rising Star by Super Lawyers, recognized for her pro bono work for KCMBF's Military Matters, has been published in The Missouri Bar, and is involved with the Association for Women Lawyers and Johnson County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Tyse Samani
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Tyse Samani-Marshall is a experienced trial attorney and certified mediator with more than a decade of experience handling complex family law and personal injury litigation. Licensed in both Kansas and Missouri, she has been recognized by Super Lawyers in both states and selected to the Super Lawyers Rising Stars list every year since 2023 for her professional achievements and peer recognition.

As a trial attorney, Tyse represents clients in complex divorce litigation, high-conflict custody disputes, child support matters, paternity actions, private adoptions, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, and the modification and enforcement of court orders. She approaches each case with careful analysis and courtroom readiness, understanding that leverage is created through preparation, credibility, and experience.

Her personal injury practice reflects the same litigation-driven philosophy. She represents clients in serious automobile collisions, premises liability claims, insurance bad-faith actions, medical negligence, and dog-bite injuries. Over the course of her career, she has secured significant recoveries for her clients and remains committed to holding negligent parties and insurers accountable through decisive advocacy.

Separate from her litigation practice, Tyse serves as a professional mediator. Through her independent mediation services, she works with attorneys and parties to resolve complex family law disputes. Drawing on more than ten years of courtroom experience, she brings structure, neutrality, and practical legal insight to the mediation process.

Whether litigating or mediating, Tyse approaches every matter with strategy, focus, and unwavering determination. Her mission is clear: to deliver outcomes that truly serve her clients’ goals and safeguard their future.

attorneys.name: Philip G. Scanlon
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Phil Scanlon has successfully represented thousands of criminally accused in jurisdictions across the State of Missouri at the trial and appellate level. Mr. Scanlon has handled every type of criminal charge and is well versed in criminal law and procedure.

Mr. Scanlon is unmatched by his peers in trial and appellate experience. He has conducted jury trials in both urban and rural jurisdictions and is renowned for his trial advocacy and legal aptitude. Passionate, boisterous, and intense, Mr. Scanlon is relentless in defense of those he represents.

Mr. Scanlon is a native of St. Louis. He was a scholarship athlete and completed his undergraduate education at William Jewell College in Liberty, Missouri. While attending St. Louis University School of Law, he was selected to serve the United States Army as a civil servant with the Trial Defense Unit in Fort Riley, Kansas. After obtaining his Juris Doctorate, he served as a Missouri State Public Defender in the 24th Circuit. He gained copious trial experience while an associate attorney at Taaffe & Associates located in downtown St. Louis. He has been with Sindel Noble since November 2019.

Mr. Scanlon is licensed in the State of Missouri, the Federal Eastern District of Missouri, the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals. and the United States Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Anne W. Schiavone
attorneys.practice_type: Product Liability Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
My entire legal life has been in spent in Kansas City. The first four years in the profession were spent working for defense firms. I defended corporations in environmental disputes, product defect and personal injury cases. After four years I took my knowledge of the law, and the defense perspective and opened a personal injury and employment firm. We only represent individuals. There is no comparison between working for a corporation and working for an individual. I have truly enjoyed each client with whom I have had the opportunity to work.

The scope of my practice includes representing plaintiffs who have been injured by the negligence or intentional act of others. This encompasses claims involving injury from products such as medical devices, single event personal injury claims, as well as claims involving discrimination in employment or wrongful termination. I also represent adult and child victims of sexual abuse/assault.

In addition to my day-to-day litigation practice I have the honor of serving on several committees. In 2016 I was appointed to the Executive Committee of The Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys. We work to protect the civil justice system and the 7th amendment. This commitment includes making frequent visits to our state Capitol to advocate for and protect the rights of individuals within our state. I am honored to currently serve as the President of MATA. I am one of only five females to hold this position in the 70 plus years of the organization. I am a state delegate in the American Association for Justice, a national organization working to promote justice for injured persons, and to safeguard victims’ rights.

In 2017 I was appointed to the Executive Committee of a Multi District Litigation pending in The United States District Court of New Hampshire. I along with four colleagues from various parts of the country were tasked with overseeing the litigation of thousands of cases pending in the MDL relating to hernia mesh products. The litigation concluded in 2023. In September of 2023, I was appointed to the Executive Committee of a Multi District Litigation pending in The United States District Court of Arizona. The current litigation involves implantable port catheters.

I was privileged to serve on the merit selection panel for the reappointment of a magistrate judge for the United States District Court of the Western District of Missouri as well as the selection of a new magistrate to fill a vacancy within the Court. In May of 2023, I was awarded the Distinguished Counselor Award from the Kansas City Metropolitan Bar Association which recognizes a member who demonstrates professionalism, collegiality, and courtesy in the practice of law. I enjoy practicing in the Kansas City legal community and have met many outstanding attorneys in my 25 years of practice.

attorneys.name: Craig Anthony Schlapprizzi
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Since graduating from Washington University Law School in 2009, Craig Schlapprizzi has earned the respect of his coworkers and clients by tackling a broad range of personal injury cases from auto and trucking crashes, to medical malpractice and premises liability, to contract claims and appellate work.

In his first year practicing law, Craig achieved judgments, verdicts and settlements in excess of $1.6 million. He was the lead trial lawyer in two jury trials; one a wrongful death case, the other a commercial trucking crash. Both resulted in substantial jury verdicts for his clients.

In 2011, he teamed with his father, sister and Linda Powers in two major personal injury suits, both involving catastrophic injuries. The cases settled before trial for $2.5 million each.

For the second year, Craig is serving on the New Lawyers Committee, Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys (MATA).

Craig says he always wanted to be an attorney and represent individuals not corporations. He is honored to be part of this noble profession and to be learning from his father and mentor, who Craig considers to be the best trial lawyer he has ever seen.

Education & Sports:

Craig played football for Dartmouth College where he earned his bachelor's degree before attending Washington University School of Law.

attorneys.name: John J. Schirger
attorneys.practice_type: Banking Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
John has represented businesses and individuals nationwide in disputes concerning breach of contract, fraud, business torts, consumer protection, insurance and reinsurance, securities and commodities, whistle-blower claims, and environmental matters. He also has significant experience in personal injury and wrongful death cases on both the plaintiff and defense side. Over the years John has successfully handled cases in federal or state courts in over 20 states, has argued before federal and state appellate courts, and has represented parties in AAA and Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) arbitrations.

John began his career at a large regional law firm where he was elected partner after four years of practice. After only five years of practice, he obtained an "AV" rating from law publisher Martindale-Hubbell, the highest rating a lawyer can receive for competence and ethics. John has been named a Top 100 Missouri & Kansas Super Lawyer, and Best of the Bar by the Kansas City Business Journal.

John is currently representing clients in a wide variety of cases involving business and commercial disputes, securities litigation matters, and class actions. In these cases, his clients include business owners, individuals and family members, investors including community banks and hedge funds, and members of the Forbes 400. John is known for his disciplined and thorough approach in cases, but also for being practical and creative in resolving disputes. One client recently stated: "John has the ability to sort through complex information and decide what is most important. He'll develop a litigation plan, and execute on it, but looks for opportunities to creatively resolve a case."

For a general description of cases in which John has been involved, please refer to the Representative Cases section of this website.

John is a native of Rockford, Illinois, and now lives in Mission Hills, Kansas with his wife and two daughters.

attorneys.name: Paul L. Schmitz
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Litigation Lawyers in St Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Paul leads the criminal law practice at UGBB. His practice benefits from a prior career in law enforcement. He served at the State of Missouri Board of Probation and Parole holding positions as a probation and parole officer and later in management. The experience allowed Paul to become thoroughly familiar with the criminal justice adjudication process from the initiation of proceedings through sentencing with a vision towards the best possible outcome. Accordingly, Paul provides a comprehensive approach in his assistance to clients who face criminal charges ranging from minor infractions up to serious felony indictments. Paul has experience handling cases involving violent crimes, drug crimes, sex crimes, property crimes, traffic violations, white collar crime, misdemeanors, felonies and many other criminal charges.

Paul successfully argued cases before the Missouri Court of Appeals in the Eastern and Western Districts of Missouri and is capable of building defenses in opposition to criminal accusations at each stage of the legal process.

Paul also coordinates representation with other UGBB attorneys in a broad range of civil litigation matters.

Paul's varied experience, empathy in recognition of the difficult situations each of his clients face and his passion for meeting the needs of his clients are all factors that contribute to strong legal representation. All this, when combined with a spirit of collaboration, allow him to bring a comprehensive perspective to his clients' cases. As one of the firm's partners, Paul seeks practical, cost-effective resolutions, while keeping in mind the long-term implications of each matter.

I have been a practicing attorney since June 4, 1979. During that period of time, I have practiced in all areas of the law, except federal taxation. I’ve handled criminal misdemeanors and felonies. I’ve conducted civil litigation, prepared wills, filed estates, drafted contracts, acted as a mediator, acted as guardian ad litem, conducted discovery, prepared for trial, conducted trials, filed appeals before the Eastern District Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of the State of Missouri. attorneys.name: Carrie S. Schormann
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Saint Peters, MO
attorneys.bio:
Carrie Schormann focuses on estate planning, estate and trust administration and estate and trust litigation for families. Her experience includes all types of basic and advanced estate planning, formation of business entities, private foundations and charitable trusts. Carrie prepares estate and gift tax returns and other fiduciary tax returns for her clients. She also represents personal representatives and trustees in connection with estate and trust administration matters.

Carrie works collaboratively with other professionals (such as accountants and financial advisors) so that the client's needs are met in a holistic and comprehensive manner.

Representative Experience

Estate Planning

Carrie will assist you in developing and achieving your estate planning objectives while minimizing estate, gift and income taxes and potential family conflicts. From implementing creditor protection planning to creating a comprehensive estate plan for multiple generations of your family, Carrie can assist you in structuring an estate plan that incorporates your goals and objectives. Carrie listens to her clients to craft unique resolutions to complex estate planning issues.

Carrie has significant experience in assisting clients in implementing lifetime gifting strategies to transfer significant wealth to the next generation, including the transition of family business assets.

Antenuptial agreements and postnuptial agreements can be an important part of an individual's estate plan. Carrie routinely assists in negotiating and drafting these agreements for her clients.

Estate and Trust Administration

The loss of a loved one is a difficult time for many people. Carrie is experienced in assisting families in all states of estate and trust administration to enable clients to navigate the complex process of collecting and distributing assets after death. Carrie will assist you in completing the administration process quickly and efficiently. Carrie has extensive experience working with surviving spouses learning to manage their wealth for the first time.

Estate and Trust Litigation

Carrie works directly with individual and corporate fiduciaries to resolve disputes involving the fiduciary's administration of estate and trust assets and the interpretation of provisions of estate planning documents. Carrie also works with beneficiaries to resolve family disputes involving estate and trust assets.

Carrie advises clients on the proper procedure to reform trusts to better meet the needs of the beneficiaries and the goals of the grantor, and she assists clients through any court proceeding necessary to obtain approval of reformation.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey Sedlacek Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Clayton, MO
attorneys.bio:
Family law matters such as divorce are difficult for anyone to face. When these issues arise, it is important to have someone on your side who will work to protect your rights and be there for you when you need it the most. Jeffrey Sedlacek is a compassionate Senior Associate Attorney with Stange Law Firm. Located in our Clayton, MO, family law office, he is ready and able to assist individuals throughout St. Louis County, MO, and the surrounding areas.

Jeffrey attended law school at St. Louis University School of Law, earning his Juris Doctor degree with a Health Law Certificate. Before law school, he attended Southern Illinois University – Edwardsville, where he earned both his Master of Business Administration in Management and Information Systems Specialization and his Bachelor of Science in Computer Management and Information Systems.

Joining the St. Louis divorce lawyers at Stange Law Firm, Jeffrey brings a strong background in compliance, risk management, and client advocacy. Most recently, he served as Compliance Manager at Gateway Regional Medical Center, where he guided patients, providers, and staff through the resolution of sensitive complaints and grievances with compassion and care. In that role, he also oversaw risk management efforts, streamlined record-keeping, and ensured that policies and agreements aligned with legal and ethical standards. Before that, Jeffrey managed compliance programs at Anderson Healthcare and Home State Health, where he advised on complex regulatory matters, supported clients and providers in resolving disputes, and helped strengthen systems to protect those relying on essential services. Earlier in his career, he worked directly with individuals as an attorney, advising clients on Social Security Disability claims, developing legal strategies, and managing high caseloads with attention to detail and empathy. His career reflects a consistent commitment to helping people navigate difficult situations while protecting their rights and interests.

Civil litigation includes commercial, business, landlord/tenant, civil rights and police brutality.

The University of Missouri-Columbia awarded Mr. Shipley a Bachelor of Arts, with Honors in Economics, degree in 1982, and a Juris Doctor, Cum Laude, degree in 1985. He was a member of the Missouri Law Review and was inducted into Phi Beta Kappa and The Order of the Coif.

Mr. Shipley is admitted to practice in the Missouri Bar, the United States Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit, the United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, the United States District Court for the Western District of Missouri, and the United States District Court for the District of Kansas.

Following graduation from law school, Mr. Shipley served as a law clerk to the Honorable Howard F. Sachs, U.S. District Court, Western District of Missouri. After practicing with two smaller firms in Clay County for over fifteen years, he founded the Law Offices of Michael S. Shipley, LLC, in 2003. He has been an officer and Director of the Clay County Bar Association for the last several years, and is a member of the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He has published articles in the Missouri Law Review and in Barrister magazine.

attorneys.name: Anthony G. Simon
attorneys.practice_type: Patent Litigation Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Anthony G. Simon is a member of Simon Law in St. Louis, Missouri, where he also serves as founding attorney of the firm's Intellectual Property Group. A top-rated, award-winning lawyer with more than 28 years of legal experience, Mr. Simon represents a diverse range of individual and business clients across the country who have legal needs involving patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets and other intellectual property matters, along with business litigation, class actions and antitrust litigation.

Over the course of his career, Mr. Simon has achieved notable success representing some of the largest companies in America, including Google, Microsoft, Yahoo and other Fortune 500 corporations. A seasoned litigator, he has served as lead counsel in numerous trials in state and federal courts throughout the nation, and he has extensive experience handling appeals, as well as pretrial and preliminary hearings.

No matter how complex his clients' issues are, Mr. Simon delivers passionate, personalized counsel aimed at helping his clients achieve the favorable outcomes they expect and deserve as efficiently and cost-effectively as possible. Recognized for his exemplary professionalism and outstanding legal abilities, he holds an AV Preeminent peer review rating* from Martindale-Hubbell, and The Best Lawyers in America voted him St. Louis Patent Litigation Lawyer of the Year for four consecutive years. Furthermore, he also received the Lifetime Achievement Award from America's Top 100 Attorneys for Missouri.

A 1988 graduate of the University of Notre Dame, Mr. Simon obtained his Juris Doctor cum laude from Saint Louis University School of Law in 1991. A registered patent attorney with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, Mr. Simon holds his license to practice in Missouri and Illinois, as well as before various U.S. District Courts across the nation. He is also admitted to practice before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 1st, 2nd, 8th and Federal Circuits, along with the U.S. Supreme Court.

Fully committed to his practice, Mr. Simon is an active member of several local, state and national legal organizations, including the Missouri Association of Trial Attorneys, The Lawyers Association of St. Louis, the American Bar Association and the American Association for Justice, among his other professional affiliations. He has also published articles on topics involving intellectual property infringement and other related subjects for the St. Louis Bar Journal.
