attorneys.name: Richard E. Walker
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Town and Country, MO
attorneys.bio:
Richard E. Walker concentrates his practice on defending person's accused of DWI and other crimes. Richard also has a great deal of knowledge and experience in creating Gun Trusts for gun owners.

Mr. Walker served as a police officer from 1998 to 2013, and was a member of the St. Charles County DWI Task Force for the majority of that time. During his police career he arrested approximately 1000 impaired drivers. During that time, Richard received extensive training in DWI/DUI Enforcement, Motor Vehicle, Commercial Motor Vehicle, and Motorcycle Accident Reconstruction, Sobriety Checkpoint Supervision, and Field Training. He was a Drug Recognition Expert and Instructor (DRE) as well as a DWI Detection and Standardized Field Sobriety Testing Instructor. Richard's experience in these areas provides him with the very unique ability to evaluate the performance of police officers when conducting police investigations and to effectively cross-examine police officers during trial.

Richard graduated cum laude from Lindenwood University. He worked his way through law school while serving as a full time police officer. Mr. Walker is a graduate of St. Louis University School of Law. He is a member of the Missouri Bar and the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Richard served in the US Army. He was a graduate of the U.S. Army JFK Special Warfare Center and School for Psychological Operations, Fort Bragg, NC. Richard later left the Army after receiving a medical discharge (honorable). Richard's interests include riding his motorcycle, reading, and spending time with his wife and two children.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Richard E. Walker concentrates his practice on defending person's accused of DWI and other crimes. Richard also has a great deal of knowledge and experience in creating Gun Trusts for gun owners.

Mr. Walker served as a police officer from 1998 to 2013, and was a member of the St. Charles County DWI Task Force for the majority of that time. During his police career he arrested approximately 1000 impaired drivers. During that time, Richard received extensive training in DWI/DUI Enforcement, Motor Vehicle, Commercial Motor Vehicle, and Motorcycle Accident Reconstruction, Sobriety Checkpoint Supervision, and Field Training. He was a Drug Recognition Expert and Instructor (DRE) as well as a DWI Detection and Standardized Field Sobriety Testing Instructor. Richard's experience in these areas provides him with the very unique ability to evaluate the performance of police officers when conducting police investigations and to effectively cross-examine police officers during trial.

Richard graduated cum laude from Lindenwood University. He worked his way through law school while serving as a full time police officer. Mr. Walker is a graduate of St. Louis University School of Law. He is a member of the Missouri Bar and the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Richard served in the US Army. He was a graduate of the U.S. Army JFK Special Warfare Center and School for Psychological Operations, Fort Bragg, NC. Richard later left the Army after receiving a medical discharge (honorable). Richard's interests include riding his motorcycle, reading, and spending time with his wife and two children.

attorneys.name: Curtis C. Wall
attorneys.practice_type: Construction litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Curtis is an Associate Attorney with Long & Robinson, LLC, where he focuses his practice on construction litigation and related commercial disputes. He draws on a strong blend of technical training and investigative experience to help clients navigate complex claims involving construction defects, non-payment, mechanic's liens, foreclosures, job-site incidents, contract performance, and project-management issues. His background enables him to assess problems from multiple angles—legal, operational, and technical—allowing him to develop strategic solutions aligned with clients’ business goals.

Before attending law school, Curtis completed the Master Automotive and Master Diesel Technology programs at Nashville Auto-Diesel College (now Lincoln Tech). These programs provided an analytical and technical investigative approach that focuses on the challenges and operational realities faced by project owners, contractors, and subcontractors.

Curtis’s experience as a former law enforcement officer further strengthens his investigative approach to litigation. As a community patrol officer who advanced to the rank of corporal, he responded to high-risk situations and conducted detailed investigations, including accident and incident scene analysis—skills that translate directly to investigating claims, documenting site conditions, evidence preservation, and liability assessments.

Prior to joining Long & Robinson, LLC, Curtis practiced with Midwest litigation firms representing clients in a range of civil matters from catastrophic injuries to multi-million dollar construction defect and contribution & indemnity claims. Curtis joined Long & Robinson, LLC, to focus his practice and development on construction and real estate matters. He earned his J.D. from the University of Missouri–Kansas City School of Law and is admitted to practice in Missouri and Kansas, with additional admissions to the United States District Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Missouri.

attorneys.name: David G. Waltrip
attorneys.practice_type: Civil/Business/Contract Litigation Lawyers in Saint Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
David G. Waltrip, was born in Jacksonville, Illinois.

David has been admitted to the Illinois Bar since 1984 and the Missouri Bar since 1985. He has also been admitted to practice in the federal courts before the United States District Courts for the Eastern District Missouri, (1985); the Southern District of Illinois, (2002); the Central District of Illinois (2015); the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals, (1985); the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, (2003); and the United States Court of Military Appeals, (1988).

David received a Bachelor of Science degree from MacMurray college in 1976. While attending college, David served as the legislative aide to Illinois State Representative Thomas C. Rose and upon completion of his college education was commissioned as a Second Lieutenant in the United States Marine Corps. Following active duty with the United States Marine Corps from 1976 to 1981, David received his Juris Doctor degree from Southern Illinois University in 1984.

Upon graduation from Law School, David served as an assistant State's Attorney for Jackson County, Illinois. During that time, David tried over 150 bench and jury trials ranging from misdemeanor to Attempted Murder cases. In 1985, David joined other fellow Marine Corps officers in the practice of law in St. Louis, Missouri. Since 1985, David has been a member of law firms in St. Louis and primarily focuses his practice in civil matters.

David has handled civil, criminal, and military matters as lead counsel in both federal and state courts throughout the United States and has represented a myriad of clients in various states.

From 1976 through August, 1981, David served on active duty with the United States Marine Corps. David resigned his regular commission in the Marine Corps and took a Reserve Commission where he completed his duty with the United States Marine Corps Reserve as a Major in 1999. David received the Navy Commendation Medal and other medals, decorations and citations resulting from his active duty and reserve duty with the Marine Corps.

David is a member of the Missouri Bar, the Illinois Bar, the St. Louis County Bar Association, and formerly the Bar Association of Metropolitan St. Louis. David served on the Executive Committee of the St. Louis County Bar and was the President of that organization in 1995. David was selected as the Outstanding Young Lawyer of St. Louis County in 1990. David continues to be active with the St. Louis County Bar.

From 1986 to 2019, David taught Business Law at Washington University, (University College). David has served as a member of the Board of Directors for the USO of Missouri from 2009 through 2021 during which time David served as the President of the Board from 2013 through 2014 and as Chairman of the Board from 2015 through 2016.

David practices in various areas of law which include: Civil Litigation in both State and Federal Court; Appellate Law; Business Law; Business Formations; Sale of Business; Business Torts; Commercial Litigation; Business Litigation; Employment contracts; Non-Compete Contracts; Bankruptcy; Business Planning; Contract Development and Review; Mold Remediation Litigation; Mortgage Litigation; Real Estate; Real Estate Contracts for Residential and Commercial Property; Personal Injury including Automobile Accidents; Trucking Accidents; Construction Accidents; Premises Liability; Accidents resulting form negligence of others; Slip and Fall; Wrongful Death; Medical Malpractice; Accounting Malpractice; Domestic Relations Law including Divorce; Dissolution of Marriage; Family Law; Adoptions; Child Support; Child Custody; Visitation Rights; Modification of Judgments and Decrees; Parental Relocation; Complex Division of Marital Property; Antenuptial Agreements; Annulments; Military Divorce; Military Law.

attorneys.name: Matthew Watkins
attorneys.practice_type: Business Torts Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Matt Watkins is an attorney at Edgar Law Firm, LLC, based in Kansas City, Missouri. The Firm was founded in 2002 to provide clients with the responsive, personal service they require in high-stakes, complex litigation. Matt comes to Edgar Law Firm from a successful early career in both criminal law and civil litigation. He is an experienced trial attorney, obtaining both prosecution and defense acumen with over 40 jury trials taken to verdict.

Matt was one of youngest court leads in the history of his previous county, ultimately rising to the level of Criminal Trial Director supervising multiple prosecution teams before being recruited by a prominent Texas criminal defense firm. He was also responsible for directly training prosecutors in the areas of plea negotiation and trial strategy. He was frequently asked to directly train new police recruits on courtroom testimony, even after leaving the prosecutor's office.

Matt has also practiced defending medical malpractice claims, notably litigating cases of first impression in the 8th Circuit involving COVID-19 liability for medical practitioners. His clients directly benefit from his extensive courtroom experience that allows him to anticipate problems and execute on both short and long-term goals through the course of litigation.

Matt received his Bachelor of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice from the University of Texas at Arlington in Arlington, Texas (2011). He went on to obtain his Master of Arts in Political Science with a focus on constitutional law from the University of Texas at Dallas in Richardson, Texas (2012). He was awarded his Juris Doctor from the University of Texas School of Law (2015). Matt has been admitted to practice before the state courts in Kansas, Missouri and Texas.

Mr. Watkins is also a veteran. He spent 6 years in the United States Air Force Reserves, attaining the rank of Staff Sergeant before becoming an attorney.

In his free time, Matt enjoys playing tennis and golf, and spending time with his wife and their son.

He was frequently asked to directly train new police recruits on courtroom testimony, even after leaving the prosecutor's office.

Matt has also practiced defending medical malpractice claims, notably litigating cases of first impression in the 8th Circuit involving COVID-19 liability for medical practitioners. His clients directly benefit from his extensive courtroom experience that allows him to anticipate problems and execute on both short and long-term goals through the course of litigation.

Matt received his Bachelor of Arts in Criminology and Criminal Justice from the University of Texas at Arlington in Arlington, Texas (2011). He went on to obtain his Master of Arts in Political Science with a focus on constitutional law from the University of Texas at Dallas in Richardson, Texas (2012). He was awarded his Juris Doctor from the University of Texas School of Law (2015). Matt has been admitted to practice before the state courts in Kansas, Missouri and Texas.

Mr. Watkins is also a veteran. He spent 6 years in the United States Air Force Reserves, attaining the rank of Staff Sergeant before becoming an attorney.

In his free time, Matt enjoys playing tennis and golf, and spending time with his wife and their son.

attorneys.name: Kevin D. Wayman
attorneys.firm_name: Kevin D. Wayman Attorney at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Born in San Jose, California, Kevin D. Wayman received his Bachelor of Science - Political Science undergraduate degree in 1985, the University of Missouri - St. Louis and his Law Degree, 1988, from St. Louis University. After graduating from law school, Kevin received the position of Law Clerk to United States District Court Judges Meredith, Harper and Filippine, responsible for researching and drafting memorandum, orders and judgments for the respective US District Judges. After leaving the US District Courts, Kevin was an associate attorney for the law firm of Amelung, Wulff and Willenbrock, handling insurance defense matter in personal injury and workers’ compensation cases. Kevin handled several cases to verdict during his two year association with Amelung, Wulff and Willenbrock. After leaving the insurance defense practice, Kevin started his association with Swaney, Ram, Wayman and Healey, becoming a partner in 1997. Kevin was a partner with Swaney, Ram, Wayman and Healey until 2008, when he chose to establish his own practice concentrating in Personal Injury, Workers Compensation, Social Security and Traffic matters. Since April of 2008, Kevin’s law firm has achieved several favorable results in civil jury trials, Social Security Claims and Workers’ Compensation hearings.

Kevin’s current practice includes a concentration in matters involving Personal Injury, Worker’s Compensation, Social Security, Traffic tickets and other general matters. He has successfully litigated cases involving all aspects of Workers’ Compensation, including wrongful death, permanent total disability, and disputed repetitive trauma claims; Personal Injury claims, including automobile collisions, premises liability and wrongful death cases; Social Security claims; and, Traffic tickets. Additionally, Kevin has handled and litigated personal injury matters involving automobile collisions, premises liability and wrongful death cases.

Kevin is licensed to practice law in all Missouri Courts and is admitted to practice in the Federal District Courts and the US Court of Appeals in Missouri. Kevin is a member of the Missouri Bar and has been active in the Missouri Bar Pro-Bono program as well as the US District Courts Historical Committee.

Kevin has resided in the St. Louis area for over thirty years with his wife and four sons.

attorneys.name: Drew Weber
attorneys.practice_type: General Municipal Representation Lawyers in Saint Charles, MO
attorneys.bio:
Drew Weber is a distinguished attorney with over a decade of experience focusing on state and local government, corporate, and real estate law. As a native of St. Charles County, Drew brings not only a wealth of legal expertise but also a deep understanding of the unique needs and dynamics of the region.

Drew’s journey in the legal profession began at the University of Missouri School of Law, where he laid the foundation for his career. His extensive experience has made him a sought-after advisor and advocate for individuals and businesses navigating the complexities of real estate transactions, zoning and land use matters, and various complex corporate transactions, including mergers and acquisitions, construction contracts, and contracts for goods and services. Drew’s work in the area of real estate law has led to him being included on the Best Lawyers in America® list for Real Estate Law since 2022.

Drew also represents various local government entities, including serving as the City Attorney for the cities of Cottleville and Warson Woods, the County Counselor for Warren County, and also serving as Assistant City Attorney to four additional cities. In representing local governments, Drew incorporates his corporate and real estate practice skills to provide well-rounded guidance to governmental officials.

As a result of his extensive experience, Drew has presented seminars as a lecturer on various topics of interest for local governments, business associations, and other groups. He is adept at providing strategic guidance to businesses of all sizes, ensuring they navigate legal challenges with confidence and success. Drew’s reputation within the community is one of respect and trust. Colleagues and clients alike value his unwavering commitment to ethical standards, his dedication to achieving favorable outcomes, and his ability to build strong relationships based on trust and integrity.

attorneys.name: Dan Welsh
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Dan Welsh focuses his practice on the representation of the owners and developers of commercial real estate and the resolution of complex business disputes. His work frequently ranges from traditional real estate development and zoning work to handling the diverse legal issues that typically arise in the operation of a mature development. In the event that a development project hits a snag, Dan assists developers in resolving disputes with contractors, vendors, municipalities, and in moving projects to completion. Irrespective of the nature of the dispute, Dan utilizes a direct and practical approach that is designed to maximize the economic result for his clients. As a result, he is trusted by his clients to assist with matters that range from routine day-to-day problem solving to complex, high-stakes, "bet the company" litigation.

Dan is one of the pioneers in representing individuals and businesses with their entry into Missouri's newly created medical marijuana market. Dan helps cannabis startups with all facets of their initiatives, including corporate formation, capitalization, joint ventures, mergers, acquisitions, pre-application work, location site control, zoning, interfacing with government relations and lobbyists, license application and related services designed to maximize application success. Dan also assists experienced cannabis operators, local governments, lending institutions, vendors, investors, landlords and developers with their entry into Missouri's newly created market.

In addition to his real estate and cannabis related practice, Dan also represents a wide array of entities including tech startups, software developers, lending institutions, bankruptcy trustees, design professionals, sports agents and athletes. Dan is an active participant in the region's ag tech and plant science community, and is a member of the firm’s management committee.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Missouri Kansas Super Lawyers – Rising Star 2010, 2013, 2014, 2015

attorneys.name: Floyd A. White Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of F. A. White, Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense - Federal and State Felony & serious misdemeanors Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
F.A. White, Jr. | Criminal Defense Counsel

Aggressive Advocacy. Strategic Defense. Proven Results.

In the high-stakes arena of serious criminal litigation, there is no substitute for experience and a relentless work ethic. F.A. White, Jr. has built a reputation in Kansas City and throughout Missouri as a formidable advocate for those facing the most daunting allegations the government can bring. He does not merely "handle" cases; he builds comprehensive, battle-ready defenses designed to protect his clients' liberty and future.

A Command of High-Stakes Criminal Litigation

F.A. White, Jr. focuses his practice on complex, high-consequence criminal matters in both State and Federal courts. He understands that when a client is charged with a serious felony, they are often facing a well-funded prosecution and life-altering penalties. His approach is rooted in a "no stone unturned" philosophy—combining clinical attention to detail with a sophisticated understanding of constitutional law.

His courtroom experience spans the full spectrum of serious criminal defense, including:

Violent Crimes & Homicide: Defending those accused of the most serious offenses with rigorous investigation and expert witness coordination.

Federal & Large-Scale Narcotics: Navigating the complexities of conspiracy charges and mandatory minimum sentencing.

White Collar & Internet Crimes: Utilizing forensic analysis to dismantle sophisticated digital and financial allegations.

Sex Crimes & Gun Violations: Providing a shield against charges that carry permanent social and legal consequences.

The Tactical Advantage

What sets Mr. White apart is his tactical tenacity. He is a student of the evidence, meticulously scouring discovery to identify procedural errors, constitutional violations, and evidentiary weaknesses that others might overlook. Whether he is arguing a motion to suppress or delivering a closing argument to a jury, his presence is defined by an unwavering commitment to his clients' rights.

Beyond the Courtroom

While his reputation is built on aggressive litigation, Mr. White is equally known for his judicious counsel. He recognizes the immense psychological and personal weight of a criminal indictment. He provides a direct, transparent, and compassionate environment where clients are empowered with the information they need to make critical decisions.

F.A. White, Jr. stands ready to take control of the narrative and fight for your second chance. From securing expungements to defending your life in a capital case, his mission remains the same: to provide the elite representation necessary to restore your freedom and your future.

attorneys.bio:
Steven joined Wichmer & Groneck after graduating cum laude from Washington University in St. Louis in 2009, where he received the Henry H. Furth Scholar in Law Award and Excellence in Oral Advocacy Award. His practice has focused almost exclusively on immigration law ever since. Now a principal member of the firm, Steve routinely assists clients seeking to obtain visas to the U.S. before the Department of State and in pursing family-based and employment-based petitions as well as naturalization and asylum applications with United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), including appearing with clients at interviews and examinations under oath. In addition, Steve has a robust practice in defending clients faced with deportation from the U.S., representing them in efforts to prevent removal and obtain legalization in proceedings before the Immigration Court and Board of Immigration Appeals. Steve is also a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA).

attorneys.name: John L Wilbers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
A member of the Missouri, Illinois, and Montana Bar, John earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Missouri-Columbia School of Law and his Masters of Business Administration from the University of Missouri Crosby School of Business. John also holds a diploma from the prestigious Bryce Harlow Institute on Business and Government Affairs from Georgetown University.

In addition to his collegiate studies, John played Division 1 Tennis, served as Sigma Chi Fraternity Rush Chairman, and served as a Student Senator to the University of Missouri student body. During law school, John served on the law school Honor and Ethics Committee, served as a T.A. to Professor Attorney John Swenson in teaching Business Law to undergraduates, and clerked for the Missouri Supreme Court.

Upon graduation from law school, John worked with a nationally recognized personal injury law firm and represented injured railroad workers across the United States pursuant to the Federal Employers’ Liability Act (FELA).

John has practiced law for almost two decades, and in doing so has earned the respect of judges, colleagues, and clients. In 2015, John was named Missouri Lawyers Weekly Up and Coming Attorney, and in 2016, was named a Rising Star by Missouri Kansas Super Lawyers. Only 2.5% of practicing attorneys are selected as Rising Stars. In 2017, John was recognized as a Super Lawyer, and has received the same distinguished honor in 2018 and 2019. Super Lawyers is an exclusive list, recognizing no more than 5% of practicing attorneys in Missouri, and is awarded based on peer recognition.

John is a member of the exclusive Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, due to his numerous sizeable settlements and jury verdicts in obtaining compensation for individuals or families who have sustained serious or catastrophic injuries. In 2015, John obtained the fourteenth highest jury verdict in Missouri in obtaining a $11,500,000.00 judgment on behalf of a man severely injured due to the recklessness of an intoxicated driver. Recently, John obtained financial compensation in reaching a confidential settlement for the family of a man killed in the nationally covered Duck Boat sinking on Table Rock Lake.

In addition to serving individuals and families who have sustained injury and financial loss, John believes that it is important to invest in the community in which he operates. John serves on the Board of Directors for the Soulard School, a charter school located in historic Soulard in the City of St. Louis, that embraces diversity as the cornerstone of education and development. John also invests time and has donated thousands of dollars to the Outreach Center in Hayti, Missouri, that provides a safe and structured environment for children each day after school. John’s endowment provides hundreds of children, grades K-12, with meals, school supplies, and sports and music activities, leagues, and training. John and his staff also adopt numerous families in need over the holiday season through the St. Louis County Adopt a Family program, amongst many other important non-profits that he supports.

John and his wife Laura have three children, Lillyan, Carmody, and John Jr., and are members of St. Gerard Majella Parish. John is the son of the late L.H. “Bud” Wilbers, 1932-2014, who served the country in the Army as a Forward Observer during the Korean War, and who served our community through the practice of law for fifty two (52) years.

attorneys.name: Joe Fredrick Willerth
attorneys.practice_type: Municipal Corporation - Land and Zoning Lawyers in Lee's Summit, MO
attorneys.bio:
Joe F. Willerth is a member in the firm of Kapke & Willerth L.L.C. of Independence, Missouri, engaged in a broad suburban law practice for over thirty years in the area of business and civil litigation, real estate, and personal injury law.

Mr. Willerth received his undergraduate degree in Industrial Management at Purdue University in 1970. Joe received his J.D. degree at the University of Missouri at Columbia in 1973. Joe's first employment from law school was a prestigious position as being a law clerk to the Honorable Fred L. Henley at the Missouri Supreme Court where he received an excellent background in review of litigation and appellate practice.

Mr. Willerth was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 1973 and is admitted to practice before the United States District Court, Western District of Missouri, and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Willerth has been engaged in the general practice of law in Eastern Jackson County, Missouri with a substantial number of consumer and real estate clients and real estate matters in Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown and Raymore, where he serves as City Attorney. In the area of real estate and construction litigation he has been counsel for numerous corporations, including banks, realtors, title companies, and many major homes associations.

Mr. Willerth is the author of two articles namely, "Ethical Dilemmas for Municipal Attorneys" in November of 2003, and "Subdivision Covenants, Regulations and Restrictions", UMKC Law Journal 1990. He has also frequently taught in Continuing Legal Education for attorneys and surveyors on trial techniques, real estate issues, including land surveying, mediation and arbitration. Mr. Willerth was the guest lecturer and instructor at the statewide Missouri Association of Land Surveyors at their conventions on May 12, 2007 and March 22, 1996. Mr. Willerth was an instruction on Road and Access Law on October 2, 2008 for the National Business Institute. Mr. Willerth taught and lectured as to legal issues involving Missouri local governments in November of 2003. Mr. Willerth also was an instructor at the Annual Real Estate Institute on May 19, 2005 on the topic of handling defects in new home construction and existing home sales. Mr. Willerth was also a lecturer at Land Use & Zoning Law Litigation Seminar on July 10, 2006 in which he authored an article on A Judicial Appeals of Administrative Zoning Decisions.

attorneys.name: Holli Dobler Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Holli Williams is a trial lawyer with significant experience representing clients in construction-defect disputes, commercial litigation, and first-party and third-party insurance coverage matters. She regularly advises general contractors, subcontractors, developers, property owners, and businesses navigating complex disputes involving workmanship issues, contract performance, coverage positions, and allocation of risk.

Holli began her career in litigation before transitioning into commercial real estate finance, where she closed multimillion-dollar transactions involving commercial developments, asset dispositions, and structured lending arrangements. This transactional experience deepened her understanding of underwriting, deal structure, and contractual risk distribution — insights she now leverages in litigation to evaluate claims, damages, and exposure with precision.

At Long & Robinson, LLC, Holli’s practice spans state and federal courts, arbitrations, and mediations. She is known for her disciplined case strategy, thorough preparation, and ability to translate technical construction and insurance issues into clear, actionable guidance for clients and decision-makers. Holli’s approach is grounded in practical solutions, efficient resolution, and a focus on delivering measurable value.

Her representative work includes:

Defending and prosecuting multi-party construction-defect claims involving commercial, industrial, and multifamily projects

Litigating insurance coverage disputes involving CGL policies, additional insured issues, trigger and allocation disputes, and exclusions affecting construction claims

Handling commercial contract disputes and business tort claims

Advising clients on contract drafting, risk mitigation, and claims positioning

Beyond her practice, Holli is a committed mother and a strategic thinker who brings focus, organization, and resilience to every endeavor.

Honors

attorneys.name: Nicholas Williams
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Crimes Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
Everyone is entitled to a fair trial and a vigorous defense. That is the basis of our justice system. It is also why Nicholas Williams became a lawyer.

Mr. Williams is a trial attorney who loves the challenge of solving problems that seemingly do not have an easy answer. He has won both criminal and civil trials. He has also successfully defended death eligible defendants on the federal and state levels. Additionally, with his background in finance, Mr. Williams has extensive experience defending clients accused of wire fraud, bank fraud, insurance fraud, and embezzlement.

Mr. Williams' cases have been covered by the New York Times, Wall Street Journal, Los Angeles Times, and Dateline NBC. In his time with KesslerWilliams, the firm has taken on some of the most high-profile cases in the St. Louis area, ranging from the white-collar defense of a sports executive to those accused of violence and sex crimes. During that same time, the firm has also taken on countless matters about which you will never read or hear.

Further, Mr. Williams is a teacher. He is passionate about teaching young lawyers and law students and serving as a resource for colleagues in his field. As a program director for the National Institute of Trial Advocacy (NITA), Mr. Williams travels the country teaching trial skills and deposition skills. He regularly lectures on jury selection and cross examination, among other areas of trial practice.

Mr. Williams is an adjunct faculty member at Emory University School of Law and Saint Louis University School of Law.

In addition to his work with NITA, Mr. Williams is a member of the American Bar Association (ABA), National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL), Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (MACDL), and The Bar Association of Metropolitan St. Louis (BAMSL).

Mr. Williams is a graduate of the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and Saint Louis University School of Law. He is licensed to practice law in the states of Missouri and Illinois, as well as the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri and United States District Court for the Southern District of Illinois.

attorneys.name: Philip L. Willman
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Liability Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
MEDICAL & HEALTH CARE LIABILITY / ENVIRONMENTAL

Philip L. Willman devotes his trial practice to defending physicians, medical schools, nurses, hospitals, nursing homes, psychologists and other healthcare providers in medical negligence and health care lawsuits and medical device manufactures in medical device lawsuits. Mr. Willman also provides representation to defendants in environmental litigation.

He obtained his Bachelors Degree, magna cum laude, from Duke University in 1975 and his Juris Doctor degree from Vanderbilt University in 1978. From 1978 to 1979 he was a Research Fellow in Environmental Law at the University of Illinois College of Law. From 1979 to 1984 he served as an Assistant Attorney General in the Environmental Control Division for the Illinois Attorney General, handling numerous trials and administrative proceedings involving civil and criminal environmental prosecution to conclusion.

Since joining the firm in 1984 Mr. Willman has specialized in professional liability defense and risk management for health care providers. He has handled the defense of medical schools, physicians, hospitals, nursing homes, nurses, psychologists, other healthcare providers and medical device manufacturers. He has tried more than 90 cases to a conclusion as lead counsel in jury trials in state and federal court, in both Missouri and Illinois. He has also provided representation in environmental lawsuits.

He has written and lectured on various topics related to risk management and medical professional liability. He has provided lectures for Washington University, Saint Louis University, St. Luke's Hospital, The Medical Protective, Medical Assurance, ProAssurance, PIC-Wisconsin and Ophthalmic Mutual Insurance Company.

Mr. Willman has been active in professional organizations dedicated to the support and improvement of the civil justice system. He has been a Director for the Missouri Organization of Defense Lawyers and Missouri State Representative for DRI. He has also been active in the education of the defense bar and its clients. He has been Program Co-Chair for the DRI Complex Medicine Seminar and Program Chair for the DRI Medical Liability Seminar. Currently he serves as Chair of the DRI Medical Liability & Health Care Law Committee.

Acknowledgement of being responsible for two of Missouri's "Top Defense Verdicts of 2008" in the Missouri Lawyers Weekly, January 26, 2009 edition.

REPRESENTATIVE CASES

Noldon v. Saint Louis University, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2009) Plaintiff claimed a University obstetrician failed to timely deliver a baby by C-section, resulting in cerebral palsy. Plaintiff claimed more than 17 million dollars in damages. The jury returned a defense verdict. The case showed how effective use of ACOG criteria can support a causation defense.

Parish v. Bond, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2008) A patient suffering from high blood pressure asserted her physician failed to manage her hypertension, resulting in a stroke and brain injury. The defense verdict was the result of using evidence of patient non-compliance as a shield against negligence claims.

Hoff v. St. John's Mercy Medical Center, St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri (2007) - A trauma patient, with a thoracic spine fracture and a seizure disorder, alleged a spine surgeon delayed surgery, resulting in his experiencing seizures and paralysis. The jury verdict for the spine surgeon was based on a medical causation defense.

Schrum, et al., v. Boardwine, St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri (2005) One of five medical professional liability cases tried against a surgeon performing spinal surgery using the BAK implantation device. Four of the cases resulted in a verdict for the surgeon, despite adverse testimony from local treating surgeons.

Hertel v. Berkowitz, Madison County, Illinois (2003) - Plaintiff claimed she developed avascular necrosis, necessitating a hip replacement, as a result of the physician's improper use of Kenalog steroidal injections. After two days of deliberation the court declared a mistrial, with the jury 10-2 in favor of the physician. The case was subsequently dismissed.

Lee v. McKee, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2002) - In this wrongful death case, plaintiffs claimed a dermatologist failed to make the diagnosis of melanoma in a patient, a young mother of two children. The plaintiffs' demand was one million dollars. The jury verdict was for the defendant. Plaintiffs rejected a settlement offer of $500,000.

Virgin v. Hopewell Center, Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District (2002) - Decision determined healthcare providers do not owe a duty to warn the general public of the mental health status of a patient and the potential danger the patient presents to the public.

Reelitz v. Washington University, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2001) - Plaintiff claimed physicians at the University transplanted a liver in a patient that resulted in her contracting hepatitis and causing death. The jury verdict, for the University, recognized how medical knowledge changes over time.

Asaro v. Cardinal Glennon, Missouri Supreme Court (2001) Missouri Supreme Court decision established limitations on emotional injury claims of parents for injuries to children.

Arrington v. Rose, Butler County Circuit Court, Missouri (1998) The family of a patient brought a wrongful death claim, asserting an anesthesiologist should have referred the patient to a vascular surgeon following cancer surgery, resulting in the patient losing both legs and then dying. The defense verdict was based on the defense of a recognized complication.

Douglas v. Saint Louis University, United States District Court, Eastern District of Missouri (1993) A son brought suit for the death of his mother who was treated for a stroke and subsequently died from a pulmonary embolism. The jury brought a unanimous verdict for the health care providers

Past President, Soulard Restoration Group

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
MEDICAL & HEALTH CARE LIABILITY / ENVIRONMENTAL

Philip L. Willman devotes his trial practice to defending physicians, medical schools, nurses, hospitals, nursing homes, psychologists and other healthcare providers in medical negligence and health care lawsuits and medical device manufactures in medical device lawsuits. Mr. Willman also provides representation to defendants in environmental litigation.

He obtained his Bachelors Degree, magna cum laude, from Duke University in 1975 and his Juris Doctor degree from Vanderbilt University in 1978. From 1978 to 1979 he was a Research Fellow in Environmental Law at the University of Illinois College of Law. From 1979 to 1984 he served as an Assistant Attorney General in the Environmental Control Division for the Illinois Attorney General, handling numerous trials and administrative proceedings involving civil and criminal environmental prosecution to conclusion.

Since joining the firm in 1984 Mr. Willman has specialized in professional liability defense and risk management for health care providers. He has handled the defense of medical schools, physicians, hospitals, nursing homes, nurses, psychologists, other healthcare providers and medical device manufacturers. He has tried more than 90 cases to a conclusion as lead counsel in jury trials in state and federal court, in both Missouri and Illinois. He has also provided representation in environmental lawsuits.

He has written and lectured on various topics related to risk management and medical professional liability. He has provided lectures for Washington University, Saint Louis University, St. Luke's Hospital, The Medical Protective, Medical Assurance, ProAssurance, PIC-Wisconsin and Ophthalmic Mutual Insurance Company.

Mr. Willman has been active in professional organizations dedicated to the support and improvement of the civil justice system. He has been a Director for the Missouri Organization of Defense Lawyers and Missouri State Representative for DRI. He has also been active in the education of the defense bar and its clients. He has been Program Co-Chair for the DRI Complex Medicine Seminar and Program Chair for the DRI Medical Liability Seminar. Currently he serves as Chair of the DRI Medical Liability & Health Care Law Committee.

REPRESENTATIVE CASES

Noldon v. Saint Louis University, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2009) Plaintiff claimed a University obstetrician failed to timely deliver a baby by C-section, resulting in cerebral palsy. Plaintiff claimed more than 17 million dollars in damages. The jury returned a defense verdict. The case showed how effective use of ACOG criteria can support a causation defense.

Parish v. Bond, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2008) A patient suffering from high blood pressure asserted her physician failed to manage her hypertension, resulting in a stroke and brain injury. The defense verdict was the result of using evidence of patient non-compliance as a shield against negligence claims.

Hoff v. St. John's Mercy Medical Center, St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri (2007) - A trauma patient, with a thoracic spine fracture and a seizure disorder, alleged a spine surgeon delayed surgery, resulting in his experiencing seizures and paralysis. The jury verdict for the spine surgeon was based on a medical causation defense.

Schrum, et al., v. Boardwine, St. Louis County Circuit Court, Missouri (2005) One of five medical professional liability cases tried against a surgeon performing spinal surgery using the BAK implantation device. Four of the cases resulted in a verdict for the surgeon, despite adverse testimony from local treating surgeons.

Hertel v. Berkowitz, Madison County, Illinois (2003) - Plaintiff claimed she developed avascular necrosis, necessitating a hip replacement, as a result of the physician's improper use of Kenalog steroidal injections. After two days of deliberation the court declared a mistrial, with the jury 10-2 in favor of the physician. The case was subsequently dismissed.

Lee v. McKee, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2002) - In this wrongful death case, plaintiffs claimed a dermatologist failed to make the diagnosis of melanoma in a patient, a young mother of two children. The plaintiffs' demand was one million dollars. The jury verdict was for the defendant. Plaintiffs rejected a settlement offer of $500,000.

Virgin v. Hopewell Center, Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District (2002) - Decision determined healthcare providers do not owe a duty to warn the general public of the mental health status of a patient and the potential danger the patient presents to the public.

Reelitz v. Washington University, St. Louis City Circuit Court, Missouri (2001) - Plaintiff claimed physicians at the University transplanted a liver in a patient that resulted in her contracting hepatitis and causing death. The jury verdict, for the University, recognized how medical knowledge changes over time.

Asaro v. Cardinal Glennon, Missouri Supreme Court (2001) Missouri Supreme Court decision established limitations on emotional injury claims of parents for injuries to children.

Arrington v. Rose, Butler County Circuit Court, Missouri (1998) The family of a patient brought a wrongful death claim, asserting an anesthesiologist should have referred the patient to a vascular surgeon following cancer surgery, resulting in the patient losing both legs and then dying. The defense verdict was based on the defense of a recognized complication.

Douglas v. Saint Louis University, United States District Court, Eastern District of Missouri (1993) A son brought suit for the death of his mother who was treated for a stroke and subsequently died from a pulmonary embolism. The jury brought a unanimous verdict for the health care providers

attorneys.name: Sophie Woodworth
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Though I grew up in the small town of Tonopah, Nevada, Kansas City has been my home for the past 30 years. I received my undergraduate degree and law degree from the University of Missouri, Kansas City. Following law school, I was a judicial law clerk for the Missouri Court of Appeals. This proved to be a valuable experience because, while I already had a broad understanding of the law, my time with the court gave me a greater understanding of the importance of legal procedure in the development of a case.

Everyone deserves quality legal representation. Unfortunately, because of an uncertainty of the process, or a negative attitude toward lawyers, many individuals with valid legal claims involving wrongful death or vehicle, workplace or property accidents never receive or even seek the representation they need and deserve. My goal, therefore, is to provide the best legal recourse under the law to those individuals seeking counsel.

If an individual has been injured because of another’s intentional or negligent actions, and that injury deprives them of their life, well-being or livelihood, I want to ensure that they and their family receive fair compensation. I do this because of a strong belief in the principles of equity and fairness, and a deep sense of satisfaction knowing my work has meant something to my clients.

attorneys.bio:
Charlie, a partner since 2008, graduated in 1998 with a B.A. from Culver-Stockton College in Canton, Missouri. Charlie received his J.D. from the University of Missouri-Columbia Law School in 2001. Charlie was admitted to the Missouri Bar in 2001, as well as the United States District Court in 2001. Charlie began his legal career in private practice in Jefferson City, Missouri. Following a move to the St. Louis area, Charlie worked in the practice area of insurance defense at a downtown St. Louis law firm.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly has been fiercely advocating for people who have been injured or are suffering with disabilities for over a decade, while working at a large law firm in Kansas City. Passionately fighting for her clients’ rights, Kimberly helped to ensure that each one of her clients attained the excellent results they deserved.

Personal Injury Attorney with a History of Securing Life-Changing Financial Awards for Her Clients

Due to her tenacious advocacy, Kimberly has received life-changing financial awards for her clients. A skilled trial attorney and an adept litigator, Kimberly has successfully argued cases in federal court and lead her clients to outstanding verdicts in numerous trials and administrative hearings. Kimberly excels at representing her clients against large corporations and government agencies. She has successfully represented consumers, debtors, tenants, survivors of domestic violence, and individuals who are sick and disabled, ensuring that their rights are protected.

Kimberly has dedicated her career to assisting those who could not afford legal services to gain access to justice. She joined Foster Wallace to continue to passionately fight for the rights of injured individuals and their families. Kimberly is dedicated to providing one-on-one attention to those who are facing complex and stressful legal situations. While helping walk her clients through every step of the litigation process, Kimberly ensures that they understand their options from start to finish.

Kimberly lives in Overland Park with her husband Jeffrey, and their four young children. In her spare time, Kimberly enjoys shuttling her kids around to taekwondo, football practice, and piano lessons, and forcing them to eat their vegetables.

attorneys.name: Michael T. Yonke
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Mike Yonke is passionate about what he does for a living. Every single day he helps people who have been injured because of someone's negligence. These people may have physical, psychological, or financial damages because of an accident, and he does everything in his power to help them get the compensation they deserve.

Passion for Law

In 1994, Mike Yonke became a lawyer. This is something he had dreamed about ever since he was a little boy. His late father was also an attorney who founded a law firm 60 years ago. Mike remembers being in court rooms at a young age watching his father aggressively fight for the rights of his clients, and he loved it. That's what he wanted to do when he grew up.

In high school, he tried out the skills he saw his father use in court by joining the debate team. He ended up doing well competing with other high schools throughout the state. Mike knew that he was on to something!

In college, Mike decided to intern at the Jackson County Prosecutor's Office. For two years, he was able to lend a hand in investigating and preparing murder cases. He was able to participate in some notorious murder trials.

The experience he gained from his time at the prosecutor's office fueled the fire inside of him to move forward towards a career in law. It wasn't long before he was working for the Missouri Attorney General Capital Case Unit. During that time, he worked on a death penalty case that was nationally publicized. The case ended in a guilty verdict.

He was eager to start law school and learn everything he could about the legal system. Besides his core curriculum, he went above and beyond to become a member of the National Trial Advocacy Team. He interned again at the Jackson County Prosecutor's Office where he was able to work on a first degree murder case and sexual assault case. These cases also ended in guilty verdicts.

With a law degree in hand, Mike decided to join his father's firm. It was where his passion was born and it is where it would grow for many years. This is when he started to handle high profile personal injury and wrongful death cases.

In 2001, he decided to break away from his father's law firm. He wanted to create his own law firm just like his father had done for himself over 60 years ago. This step that he took has brought Yonke law firm where it is today.

attorneys.name: Brandon York
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
Brandon York is a personal injury attorney with a deep-rooted passion for helping others. His father served as a police officer in Kansas City, Kansas, and his mother is a district court judge, drawing him to the legal field. Over the past five years, he has practiced civil litigation, handling dozens of bench trials and motion hearings. His multi-state bar licenses provide him with a unique understanding of how court systems vary across jurisdictions.

Brandon’s focus on personal injury law stems from personal experience. His grandparents tragically passed away in a motor vehicle accident, and his sister sustained significant injuries from a dog attack. These events have fostered an empathetic and compassionate approach to representing clients, particularly in cases involving motor vehicle accidents, premises liability, and catastrophic injuries. Brandon takes a straightforward, hands-on approach, striving to truly understand his clients’ stories and provide them with honest, direct guidance.

A Kansas City, Kansas native with Cuban roots, Brandon is a graduate of Kansas State University and the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Law. Outside of work, he enjoys Chiefs games as a season ticket holder, golfing, home renovations, and spending time with his wife and two children.

attorneys.name: John A. Young
attorneys.practice_type: General Municipal Representation Lawyers in Saint Charles, MO
attorneys.bio:
John Young is a distinguished legal professional with over two decades of unparalleled experience representing municipalities, other political subdivisions, businesses and members of the development community. With a proven track record of success and a deep understanding of the intricate world of municipal law, John is a trusted advisor.

John embarked on his legal career with a commitment to serving the interests of state and local governments and other political subdivisions. As the City Attorney for four cities, Assistant City Attorney or Special Counsel to other cities and governmental entities and his many years navigating the process of land use approvals, his extensive experience in this highly specialized field has made John a go-to authority to address the unique legal challenges of municipal law and development regulations. With a wealth of legal knowledge honed over two decades, John has adeptly guided clients through a myriad of complex state and local government issues. From regulatory compliance to land use and zoning, and public policy matters to Sunshine Law compliance, John possesses an exceptional ability to provide strategic counsel and innovative solutions.

What truly distinguishes John is not just his legal acumen but also his dedication to public service. John understands that representing and working with state and local governments requires a commitment to the greater good. This commitment has earned John a reputation as a tireless advocate for those he serves.

Over the years, John has built a legacy of trust and respect within the legal and government community. John’s unwavering commitment to ethical standards, advocacy for transparency, and ability to build strong relationships with clients and stakeholders have solidified John’s status as a trusted partner for all clients.

attorneys.name: Mary Beth Youngworth
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination Lawyers in Kansas City, MO
attorneys.bio:
I have dedicated my legal career to ensuring those who have been wronged by the actions of another find relief in the justice system. I have prosecuted complex legal and factual scenarios, through all phases of litigation, specifically adult and child sex offenses, murder, assault, robbery, child abuse/neglect, and domestic violence. I am adept at navigating the legal system, leveraging resources and engaging in mediation and settlement negotiations.

My time as a prosecutor not only honed the skill set necessary to take on the “hard” cases, it made me comfortable in the courtroom arguing cases to jury verdicts in both first and second chair positions. I developed a high level of empathy that carried over to my civil practice. My desire to ensure that those who have been wronged by the tortious, discriminatory, or negligent conduct of others drives me to dedicate my legal skills to ensuring the justice system is employed to ensure the rights of all people are upheld.

In law school, I interned with the Honorable Zel M. Fischer of the Missouri Supreme Court, participated in the prosecution and veteran’s clinic, and was recognized for excellence in advocacy in multiple moot court and mock trial competitions. Before attending law school, I served my country in the United States Army. I commissioned in the top two percent of Active Duty Appointees nationwide and was honored to be selected to serve as a helicopter pilot. I deployed in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation New Dawn, flying combat missions as an Attack Scout Helicopter Weapons Team Air Mission Commander and Pilot in Command.

My peers and supervisors describe me as tenacious and dedicated. I am passionate and will fight for my clients to get the best possible outcome. When not advocating for others, I enjoy spending time with my husband and children and squeezing in a good book on a lazy Sunday afternoon.

In law school, I interned with the Honorable Zel M. Fischer of the Missouri Supreme Court, participated in the prosecution and veteran’s clinic, and was recognized for excellence in advocacy in multiple moot court and mock trial competitions. Before attending law school, I served my country in the United States Army. I commissioned in the top two percent of Active Duty Appointees nationwide and was honored to be selected to serve as a helicopter pilot. I deployed in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom and Operation New Dawn, flying combat missions as an Attack Scout Helicopter Weapons Team Air Mission Commander and Pilot in Command.

My peers and supervisors describe me as tenacious and dedicated. I am passionate and will fight for my clients to get the best possible outcome. When not advocating for others, I enjoy spending time with my husband and children and squeezing in a good book on a lazy Sunday afternoon.

items: Witnessing your boss committing an illegal act will likely create internal conflict. Should you reveal it? Will you lose your job?
While laws have become more stringent and ongoing training is provided to staff to raise awareness, sexual harassment still exists in many workplaces.

Race and national origin should have nothing to do with your employability or the loss of your job. At the Employee Rights Law Firm — Law Offices of Mark A. Jess, L.L.C., we aggressively advocate for our clients victimized by race discrimination.

Gender discrimination can take on many forms, involving both men and women. If you suspect that your gender is a factor in your job stability or an existing hostile work environment, you need an aggressive employment law attorney at your side.
The sudden loss of a job is unsettling. Even more unsettling is the realization that your firing was actually a retaliatory discharge. You witnessed and reported an illegal activity.

attorneys.bio:
Jacob Zimmerman has been practicing law since 2001. Jacob serves as Of Counsel to NST Law Injury Attorneys. Jacob is an accomplished trial lawyer and he has tried numerous cases all across Southeast Missouri and the greater St. Louis area. Jacob has won numerous awards for his skills as a trial attorney, most notably the prestigious Charles M. Shaw Award for Excellence in trial advocacy from the Missouri Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys. The Charles M. Shaw award is presented exclusively to those exhibiting excellence in trial skills.

Furthermore, Jacob is the only attorney in southeast Missouri area listed as a Top 100 Trial Lawyer by the National Trial Lawyers, an invitation only organization. The National Trial Lawyers is a professional organization composed of the premier trial lawyers from across the country who exemplify superior qualifications as civil plaintiff or criminal defense lawyers.

Jacob attends numerous courses to stay ahead of the curve on legal issues and he has presented lectures on trial techniques, motion practice, and sex crimes. He has also trained numerous new lawyers starting their careers.

Jacob uses his litigation and trial skills to help clients who are facing difficult life decisions. He focuses his practice in areas of criminal law, DWI law, and Family law. NST Law Injury Attorneys is fortunate to have Jacob serve as Of Counsel in the Cape Girardeau office.

attorneys.name: David L. Zwart Sr.
attorneys.practice_type: Business, Estate & Tax Lawyers in St. Louis, MO
attorneys.bio:
BUSINESS, ESTATE & TAX

David L. Zwart, Sr. is the founder of Moser & Marsalek, P.C. Business, Estate, Tax Department. The BE&T Group concentrates it’s practice in the areas of general business, tax planning and representation in both estate and income tax areas, probate and real estate. The Group specializes in a wide range of business and individual issues, matters and problems.

Mr. Zwart's background is well suited for this type of practice. He is a licensed certified public accountant, has received a Masters of Law in Taxation from New York University and is a licensed real estate broker. He has served on various corporate boards, as well as charitable organizations and local government.

He is the author of "Dollar Sense for Today's Woman". This book has been distributed by a leading St. Louis trust company and used as a textbook by various Universities.

Mr. Zwart has been involved in successful estate planning for multimillion dollar estates. He has represented individuals and corporations in a wide range of income tax matters. He has represented both buyers and sellers in the purchase and sales of many businesses, including sole proprietorships, partnerships, joint ventures and limited liability companies. He has also represented both landlords and tenants in leasing and selling real estate.
